front_matter.purpose:
# Purpose of This Manual

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** operates its Community Integrated Living Arrangement (CILA) program in Illinois. A CILA is a site where 8 or fewer individuals with a developmental disability live under agency supervision (210 ILCS 135; 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120). The agency is licensed by the Illinois Department of Human Services (IDHS) Bureau of Accreditation, Licensure and Certification (BALC) under 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115 and 210 ILCS 135. Its services are paid through the Medicaid HCBS Waiver for Adults with Developmental Disabilities (IL.0350.R05.04), for which IDHS Division of Developmental Disabilities (DDD) is the operating agency and the Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS) is the Medicaid agency.

The manual is intended to:

- Give **[AGENCY NAME]** written policies and procedures that match the uniform direction for CILA licensure and operation in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.100.
- Support settings and services that promote integration and full community access, control of personal resources, privacy, dignity and respect, and freedom from coercion and restraint, as described in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.200.
- Make sure person-centered planning, individual rights, health and medication practices, restraint limits, environmental safety, staffing, background checks and training, and reporting are carried out consistently by every employee, contractor and volunteer.
- Give the governing body, BALC surveyors, DDD and other reviewers a clear record of how the agency meets its obligations.
- Use the terms defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120, including CILA, continuous supervision or support, critical incidents, DSP, Implementation Strategy, informed consent, restraint, aversive procedures and community integration, in the same way the rule does.

**This manual is a template and must be customized.** Every bracketed placeholder (such as **[AGENCY NAME]**) must be replaced with agency-specific information. Procedures must be adapted to the agency's actual organization, staffing patterns, sites and service model. Where this manual summarizes a rule, the official rule text controls. Several citations in this manual are summaries whose exact subsection must be confirmed against the official text before the manual is finalized. These are noted in the Regulatory Framework section.

**Adoption, currency and training.** The manual is not in effect until it has been reviewed and adopted by the agency's governing body (as defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120 and described in 115.320(a)). It must be kept current as laws, rules, waiver terms, IDHS/DDD guidance and agency practice change, and the adoption date and revision history must be recorded. All staff must be trained on the manual, and training must be documented, at hire or orientation, when policies change, and on an ongoing basis.

# How to Use This Manual

## Who should use it

- **Direct Support Professionals (DSPs) and other direct care staff** use it for day-to-day expectations: rights, supervision, medications, incident response, emergencies and documentation.
- **Qualified Intellectual Disability Professionals (QIDPs), nurses and Provider Support Team members** use it for person-centered planning, Implementation Strategies, health oversight and requests for additional supports.
- **Administrators and the authorized CILA agency representative** use it for licensure, personnel, background checks, training, reporting, billing and regulator communication.
- **The governing body** uses it to adopt policy, review compliance and receive input from individuals, guardians and representatives.
- **Individuals, guardians and advocates** may review the policies that affect them, including admission policies, rights and complaint processes, which must be in writing and available for review.

## Getting started

1. **Customize first.** Replace all **[AGENCY NAME]** and other bracketed placeholders. Insert agency names, titles, phone numbers, site addresses, the Rights of Individuals form, the restraint policy (if any) and the disaster preparedness plan.
2. **Confirm the rule text.** Where the Regulatory Framework section says a subsection must be pinned, check it against the official text at the linked source (JCAR or ILGA) before finalizing.
3. **Have the governing body adopt it.** Record the adoption date, the approving individuals and the effective date.
4. **Train staff.** Train all employees, contractors and volunteers on the manual. Keep sign-in sheets, content outlines and competency checks. Retrain when sections change.
5. **Keep it where staff can find it.** Keep the current version available at the agency office and at each site. Current Personal Plans and Implementation Strategies are kept at the residence.
6. **Review and update.** Review the manual at least annually and whenever a rule, waiver provision, IDHS/DDD notice or a licensing or complaint survey finding calls for a change. Keep prior versions and a revision log.

## Conventions in this manual

- Rules are cited by their exact cite text (for example, "59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.245"). Agency policy statements go beyond the rule only where the agency has chosen to do so, and those should be identified as agency policy.
- Where a rule and this manual appear to conflict, **the rule controls**. Notify the administrator and correct the manual.
- Items marked "confirm" or "verify" need agency follow-up with BALC or DDD before being relied on.
- When a situation is not covered, or staff are unsure, they contact the supervisor or on-call administrator right away. For anything involving health, safety, abuse, neglect or exploitation, staff act first to protect the individual and then report as required.

# Regulatory Framework

## Governing statutes, rules and guidance

### Licensure and program rules

- **210 ILCS 135** – Community-Integrated Living Arrangements Licensure and Certification Act. This is the statutory basis for CILA agency licensure and site certification.
- **210 ILCS 135/4** – Licensure of community developmental services agencies. It sets licensure requirements and fees. The application fee is capped at $200. The nonrefundable licensure and renewal fee follows Section 4(d), and agencies certify compliance with Section 4 in the application.
- **59 Ill. Adm. Code 115** – Standards and Licensure Requirements for Community-Integrated Living Arrangements (amended effective 5/31/2023, 47 Ill. Reg. 8485). This part-level cite is used where a paragraph was seen but its exact section or subsection was not confirmed. Those items include required record contents, admission policies in writing, life-safety compliance, current Personal Plans and Implementation Strategies kept at the residence, and surveys at renewal and for complaints. *Pin the exact section from the official text before finalizing.*
- **59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.100** – Purpose.
- **59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120** – Definitions. This section also incorporates the Part 50.10 definitions of abuse and financial exploitation.
- **59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.200** – Description. It covers settings and service principles, accessibility, person-centered planning, documented informed consent, and the exclusion of day programs from the CILA rate. *Subsection letters to be pinned.*
- **59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.205** – Respite Services for Persons with a Developmental Disability. It requires a physician statement of no contagious disease and documentation that the individual will not jeopardize others' health or safety. Respite longer than two weeks needs Department approval before the initial two weeks end, and only in emergencies.
- **59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.210** – Criteria for Participation of Individuals. Individuals must be at least 18 (an age waiver may be requested for those at least 17.5). No otherwise qualified individual may be denied placement solely on diagnosis. Admission policies must be in writing and available for review. *Subsection to be pinned.*
- **59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.214** – Individuals Requiring Additional Services and Support. The Department responds to team requests no later than ten business days after receipt. Need for non-base support hours is reviewed at least annually and reported to the Department. *Subsection letters to be pinned.*
- **59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.220** – Services and Supports. It requires a Provider Support Team (including a QIDP and a DSP, plus a nurse or other professionals as needed) and sets out the team's service functions, 24-hour availability, medication-related support and sexual health supports.
- **59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.230** – Person-Centered Planning. It covers the Implementation Strategy on Form IL462-4470 within 20 calendar days of the provider's dated signature on the Personal Plan, signature and copies, monthly QIDP review, and conditions for staying alone or accessing the community independently.
- **59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.240** – Medical Services and Medications. It covers certification under the Mental Health and DD Administrative Act and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 116, physician responsibility, examination before psychotropics, AIMS screening at least every six months and physician medication review at least every six months.
- **59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.245** – Restraints. Prone, supine and mechanical restraint are prohibited. Any use must be reported in CIRAS and to the Office of the Inspector General. Other restraint is allowed only if every listed condition is met. The agency keeps a copy of its restraint policy.
- **59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.250** – Individual Rights and Confidentiality. It covers the Rights of Individuals form (IL 462-1201) at entry and annually, contact with outside advocates, and freedom from abuse, neglect, exploitation, coercion and restraint. Seclusion, time-out and aversive procedures are prohibited.
- **59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.300** – Environmental Management of Living Arrangements. It covers inspection records, the disaster preparedness plan (reviewed annually), drills, fire extinguishers, first aid kits, telephone and poison control posting, and training new individuals within 30 days of move-in. *Subsection numbers beyond (c)(8) to be pinned.*
- **59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.310** – Geographic Location of Community-Integrated Living Arrangements. These are siting rules, including the 25% building limit and waiver requests filed before leasing, buying or taking possession.
- **59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320** – Administrative Requirements. It covers the governing body, input from individuals and guardians, licensure of employees, the DPH Health Care Worker Registry and DCFS State Central Register/CANTS checks, repeat checks every 365 days, DSP training areas, volunteer training, guardian or parent notice of abuse/neglect allegations within 24 hours, and complaint handling. *Exact paragraph letters to be pinned.*
- **59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.410** – License Application. It covers application contents and certifications, the nonrefundable fee, renewal applications due at least 120 days before expiration, notice of ownership change within 60 business days and the 18-month operational deadline.
- **59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.580** – 24-Hour Service. This section is in Subpart E (Host Family Living Arrangements). **Cite it only for host family settings.** For shift-staff homes, rely on the continuous supervision definition in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120 and the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy.
- **59 Ill. Adm. Code 120.160** – Person-Centered Planning (HCBS waiver participants, guardians, ISC agencies and provider agencies). Providers develop an Implementation Strategy within 20 calendar days of signing the Personal Plan.

### Related statutes and rules incorporated by Part 115

- **59 Ill. Adm. Code 50.10** – Definitions (abuse, neglect, financial exploitation), OIG Rule 50. Only the incorporation by reference in 115.120 has been verified. *Reporting steps and timelines in Part 50 have not been retrieved and must be confirmed from the official text before the manual's reporting procedures are finalized.*
- **740 ILCS 110** – Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act. Agencies certify compliance under Part 115, and informed consent includes consent for releases of information. *The Act text has not been reviewed for this manual.*
- **405 ILCS 5, Chapter II (Rights of Recipients)** – Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Code. Under 115.250, individual rights are protected under Chapter II, except that seclusion is not permitted.
- **225 ILCS 46** – Health Care Worker Background Check Act. Part 115 implements this Act, and 115.320(b) requires compliance. *The Act text has not been reviewed for this manual.*
- **210 ILCS 165** – Authorized Electronic Monitoring in Community-Integrated Living Arrangements and Developmental Disability Facilities Act. 115.120 defines authorized electronic monitoring by reference to this Act. *The Act text has not been reviewed for this manual.*

### Federal and Medicaid waiver requirements

- **42 CFR 441.301(c)(1)-(5)** – Person-centered planning and HCBS settings requirements. Under 115.410, CILAs serving waiver participants must meet (c)(1)-(4). Settings may not be of the type in (c)(5)(v), and provider-owned or controlled sites must meet (c)(4)(vi)(A)-(E).
- **Medicaid HCBS Waiver for Adults with Developmental Disabilities (IL.0350.R05.04)** – The 1915(c) waiver in effect January 1, 2026, under which CILA services are paid. HFS is the Medicaid agency and IDHS-DDD is the operating agency.

### IDHS/DDD guidance and notices

- **IDHS New Provider Guidance - Steps for CILA** – Background checks before hire and annually, Illinois State Police fingerprint checks reported to the Health Care Worker Registry, DSP (DD Aide) training before working alone, DSP training for anyone giving direct care more than 20% of the time, first aid/CPR and OIG Rule 50 training renewed every two years, RN requirements, and the BALC visit schedule leading to a permanent license.
- **IDHS Person-Centered Planning Process (provider timelines)** – The provider signature page is due back to the ISC within 10 calendar days of receiving the Personal Plan. The Implementation Strategy is due within 20 calendar days of the QIDP signing the Provider Signature Page.
- **IDHS Person Centered Planning Policy and Guidelines for DD Waiver Services** – Providers give the individual/guardian and ISC a copy of the Implementation Strategy. The individual or guardian signs it (the ISC does not sign or approve it). Providers make sure all billed services are identified in the Personal Plan.
- **IDHS Independent Service Coordination (ISC) Manual, Section 8.2** – The ISC has 30 calendar days after the person begins DDD Waiver services to complete Discovery and develop the Personal Plan.
- **IDHS IMPACT Provider Enrollment** – IMPACT is the Medicaid enrollment and reimbursement system. Enrollment must be completed before federal reimbursement.
- **IDHS DDD Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) Policy** – It applies to IMPACT-enrolled providers billing personal care or home health care services. From April 1, 2026, providers must keep quarterly EVV compliance above 75%. *Whether 60D/61H CILA claims are covered is unverified. Confirm with DDD.*
- **IDHS January 1, 2024 Wage/Rate Increase notice** – CILA provider agencies certify that wage increases are passed through to direct care staff.

> **Customization note:** The rules above are summarized only to organize the manual. Staff and administrators must rely on the official text. Items marked "to be pinned" or "confirm" must be resolved before adoption. The agency should also identify any local ordinances, building and fire codes, and other requirements that apply to its sites and add them here. No rule is cited in this manual unless it appears in this list.

## Regulators and contacts

| Regulator | Role | Contact |

The BALC license is the first step before Medicaid waiver enrollment. | 401 S. Clinton, 7th Floor, Chicago, IL 60607. Phone: 312-814-5310. Email: DHS.BALC@illinois.gov (listed with different capitalization in two sources; confirm with BALC). Web: https://www.dhs.state.il.us/page.aspx?item=47487 |
| **IDHS Division of Developmental Disabilities (DDD)** | Operating agency for the Adults with DD waiver. Sets CILA rate methodology and rate tables. Runs PUNS selection, IMPACT enrollment steps and EVV compliance for DDD providers. | Web: https://www.dhs.state.il.us/page.aspx?item=176268. Phone/email: **[AGENCY to add]** |
| **Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS)** | State Medicaid agency responsible for the Adults with Developmental Disabilities 1915(c) HCBS waiver (IL.0350.R05.04). | Web: https://hfs.illinois.gov/medicalclients/hcbs/dd.html. Phone/email: **[AGENCY to add]** |
| **Office of the State Fire Marshal (OSFM)** | Fire inspection and clearance. BALC submits the request to OSFM when the property is ready, and the site inspection runs within 15 working days after fire clearances and other documents are received. | **[AGENCY to add]** |

| **Independent Service Coordination (ISC) agencies** | Enroll individuals in PUNS and serve as the intake and referral channel for waiver services. | Web: https://www.dhs.state.il.us/page.aspx?item=47620. Local ISC contact: **[AGENCY to add]** |

### Other contacts individuals must be told about

Under 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.250, staff give each individual the address and telephone number of the **Guardianship and Advocacy Commission (GAC)**, the **Department's Office of the Inspector General (OIG)**, the **Department** and **Equip for Equality**. Individuals may also contact the agency's human rights committee. The contact details for these organizations were not provided in the source material. **[AGENCY to insert verified addresses and phone numbers]** and post or distribute them with the Rights of Individuals form (IL 462-1201).

### Agency internal contacts

**[AGENCY NAME]** Executive Director/Administrator: **[name, phone]** | Authorized CILA agency representative: **[name, phone]** | QIDP(s): **[name, phone]** | Nurse: **[name, phone]** | After-hours on-call: **[phone]**

citations.title: Community-Integrated Living Arrangements Licensure and Certification Act
citations.requirement: Statutory basis for CILA agency licensure and site certification. A CILA is a site where 8 or fewer individuals with a developmental disability live under agency supervision.

citations.title: Licensure of community developmental services agencies
citations.requirement: Licensure requirements and fees. Application fee is capped at $200. Rule 115.410(b) points to Section 4(d) for the nonrefundable licensure and renewal fee. Agencies certify compliance with Section 4 in the application.

citations.title: Purpose
citations.requirement: Sets uniform direction for licensure and operation of CILA agencies.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines the terms the manual must use. Key definitions: CILA (8 or fewer), Continuous supervision or support (staff physically on-site all hours individuals are present unless the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy say otherwise), Critical Incidents, DSP, Implementation Strategy, Informed consent, Coercion, Aversive procedures, Restraint, Governing body, Authorized CILA agency representative, Independent Monitor and Receiver, Community integration, Authorized electronic monitoring.

citations.title: Description
citations.requirement: CILA settings and services must support integration and full community access, control of personal resources, privacy, dignity and respect, and freedom from coercion and restraint (except as 115.245 allows). They must optimize individual initiative and autonomy and be physically accessible, with communal areas meeting ADA standards. Agencies must follow person-centered planning rules (42 CFR 441.301(c)(1)-(3), 59 Ill. Adm. Code 120, 115.230). The CILA rate excludes day programs, which are billed separately. Informed consent to participate in a CILA must be documented. Subsection letters to be pinned from the official text.

citations.title: Respite Services for Persons with a Developmental Disability
citations.requirement: Before respite, the agency requires a physician statement that the individual has no contagious disease. It also documents that the individual will not jeopardize the health or safety of others in the home. Respite longer than two weeks needs Department approval before the initial two weeks end, and only in emergencies.

citations.title: Criteria for Participation of Individuals
citations.requirement: Individuals must be at least 18 with a developmental disability and need CILA services and a supervised living arrangement. Agencies may request an age waiver for individuals at least 17.5. An agency's lack of capacity for a particular disability does not make the individual ineligible. No otherwise qualified individual may be denied placement solely on diagnosis. Admission policies must be in writing and available for review (subsection to be pinned).

citations.title: Individuals Requiring Additional Services and Support
citations.requirement: Process for team requests for additional staff resources or supports. The Department responds as soon as possible and no later than ten business days after receipt. Need for non-base support hours is professionally reviewed at least annually and reported to the Department. Subsection letters to be pinned.

citations.title: Services and Supports
citations.requirement: The agency maintains a Provider Support Team for each individual. The team includes a QIDP and a DSP, plus a nurse or other professionals as needed. The team is responsible for service functions in the Personal Plan areas the agency covers and for developing the Implementation Strategy. It provides care and supervision based on assessed needs, helps the person take part in community supports, and is available 24 hours. It advocates, helps the person keep safety and comforts, and provides counseling and crisis problem-solving. It helps with ADLs and assistive devices and helps individuals access medication information, including observing and reporting effects and side effects. It supports the individual's right to sexual health and freedom from sexual exploitation, including a decision-making capacity assessment for consent to sexual activity.

citations.title: Person-Centered Planning
citations.requirement: Agencies comply with 42 CFR 441.301(c)(1)-(3) and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 120. Within 20 calendar days of the provider's dated signature on the Personal Plan, the agency develops an Implementation Strategy on Form IL462-4470. The strategy is based on the Personal Plan and assessments, with the individual and guardian taking part (ISC as necessary). It is signed by the individual and guardian and addresses the outcomes the agency agreed to support. The individual and guardian get a copy of the strategy and its updates, and it becomes part of the record. At least monthly the QIDP reviews the strategy and documents the review. A CILA rate determination packet for intermittent supports is submitted by the ISC with the CILA agency. Individuals needing continuous supervision may stay alone or access the community independently only under specified circumstances. The provider support team must assess this, and it must be based on need and preference, not staff convenience. The strategy states the time periods and locations/time frames involved.

citations.title: Medical Services and Medications
citations.requirement: When agency employees provide medical services or medications, or supervise their administration, the agency certifies this is done under the Mental Health and DD Administrative Act and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 116. A licensed physician (MD/DO) is responsible for medical services, including prescribing. A physician examines the individual before psychotropics start. AIMS screening is done at least every six months for individuals on psychotropics. A physician reviews medications and sees the individual at least every six months, more often if a psychiatrist requires.

citations.title: Restraints
citations.requirement: Prone, supine and mechanical restraint are prohibited. Any use must be reported in CIRAS and to the Office of the Inspector General. Other restraint is allowed only if every condition is met. There must be an immediate threat of serious physical harm, with less restrictive measures proven ineffective. Restraint must be a modification in the Personal Plan, approved by the individual or guardian and the Provider Support Team, and in the behavior strategy. It needs Behavior Management/Human Rights Committee approval and a plan to reduce and eliminate it. Staff must be trained in the specific restraint, and the agency must document no medical or psychological contraindication. Staff involved in restraint not in the Personal Plan may be required to complete remediation training. The agency keeps a copy of its restraint policy.

citations.title: Individual Rights and Confidentiality
citations.requirement: The agency shares and explains the current Rights of Individuals form (IL 462-1201) at entry and annually. Rights are protected under Chapter II of the Mental Health and DD Code, and seclusion is not permitted. Individuals have the right to remain in the CILA unless they withdraw or meet 115.215 criteria. They may contact the Guardianship and Advocacy Commission, Equip for Equality, the Department's OIG, the Department and the agency's human rights committee. Staff offer help and give each individual the address and telephone number of GAC, OIG, the Department and Equip for Equality. Individuals have the right to be free from abuse, neglect, exploitation, coercion and restraint. Seclusion, time-out and aversive procedures are prohibited. Individuals may use private physicians and professionals of their choice, documented in the plan.

citations.title: Environmental Management of Living Arrangements
citations.requirement: Copies of local and State health, sanitation and environment inspections are maintained. The agency keeps a disaster preparedness plan covering disasters and public health crises, reviewed annually. Fire and disaster training records are available to DDD and BALC at the site, and corrective actions for drill or inspection deficiencies are recorded. Staff and individuals know how to react to fire, severe weather, missing persons, psychiatric and medical emergencies, poison control and deaths. Staff are trained in the location of extinguishers, first aid kits and evacuation routes. An operational telephone is accessible, with a posted list of the site phone number and nearest poison control center. Evacuation drills include actual evacuation to safe areas. At least one approved fire extinguisher has an annual inspection tag. Red Cross-standard first aid kits are checked quarterly and restocked. New individuals are trained within 30 days of moving in. Residences must comply with local building codes. Subsection numbers beyond (c)(8) to be pinned from the official text.

citations.title: Geographic Location of Community-Integrated Living Arrangements
citations.requirement: Siting rules for HCBS settings. New provider-owned or controlled sites may not be adjacent to, across from, diagonal to or behind another waiver-funded residential or day site of the same provider unless a waiver is granted. They may not be in a building that provides inpatient institutional treatment. No more than 25% of units in a building may be Department-funded CILAs owned or controlled by CILA providers. Waiver requests are filed before leasing, buying or taking possession.

citations.title: Administrative Requirements
citations.requirement: (a) Corporate, association or local-government providers have a governing body with authority over operations. Providers must have a way to get input from individuals, guardians and representatives to the governing body. (b) Employees are licensed or certified as Illinois law requires. The agency may not employ anyone (including contractors, volunteers and practitioners) until it has checked the DPH Health Care Worker Registry and the DCFS State Central Register/CANTS. It must also have received the results of the applicable registry or list, and the inquiry may not occur more than 30 calendar days before the first day of employment. Checks are repeated on a schedule that completes them every 365 days. The agency complies with the Health Care Worker Background Check Act. (d) DSPs and anyone with direct care responsibility demonstrate competence in the listed training areas (A)-(M) as part of orientation, with enough trained staff to cover absences. (e) Volunteer training applies. The section also requires the agency to notify the individual's guardian or parent of an abuse/neglect allegation within 24 hours of receiving it. Each agency must have and use a process for reporting and handling complaints. Exact paragraph letters to be pinned.

citations.title: License Application
citations.requirement: New-provider requirements must be completed within one year of requesting an application. The application certifies compliance with Section 4 of the Act, the Confidentiality Act, Part 115, 59 Ill. Adm. Code 120 and 42 CFR 441.301(c)(1)-(4). Settings must not be of the type in 42 CFR 441.301(c)(5)(v), and provider-owned or controlled sites must meet (c)(4)(vi)(A)-(E). The application requires agency policies and procedures, an organizational chart, staffing patterns and staff qualifications. The nonrefundable fee follows Section 4(d) of the Act. The renewal application is due at least 120 days before expiration after Department notice. BALC and DDD must be notified of any ownership change within 60 business days. The agency must be operational within 18 months or the application is treated as abandoned.
