policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Authorized CILA Agency Representative Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Governing body members, the Authorized CILA Agency Representative, administrators, and all managers of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To establish who holds authority and responsibility for [AGENCY NAME], so that every Community Integrated Living Arrangement (CILA) site is governed, staffed and operated in line with 210 ILCS 135 and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115, and so that individuals, guardians and representatives can give input to the people who run the agency.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is governed by a governing body that has authority over the agency and all of its programs, services, facilities and residences. The governing body appoints an Authorized CILA Agency Representative who has overall fiscal and programmatic responsibility for the agency. No CILA site serves more than 8 individuals with a developmental disability. Part 115 sets no licensure staff ratio. [AGENCY NAME] therefore sets staffing at each site from what each person's Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy require, and documents that basis. The agency gives individuals, guardians and representatives a standing way to bring input to the governing body.

definitions.definition: The body with legal authority over the agency's operations, programs, services, facilities and residences, as defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120.
The person appointed by the governing body who has overall fiscal and programmatic responsibility for the agency and who signs and dates the license and renewal applications.
A site where 8 or fewer individuals with a developmental disability live under agency supervision.
Staff physically on site during all hours individuals are present, unless the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy say otherwise.
The written plan that sets out how the supports and services in the Personal Plan will be delivered.

procedures: The governing body adopts written bylaws or an equivalent governing document that states its authority over the agency and all of its programs, services, facilities and residences. The Board Chair signs it and it is kept in the governance binder.
The governing body meets at least quarterly, or more often if its bylaws require. The Board Secretary records minutes of each meeting, including attendance, decisions and votes.

The governing body appoints the Authorized CILA Agency Representative by written resolution. The resolution names [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] or another appointee and states that the person has overall fiscal and programmatic responsibility.
The Authorized CILA Agency Representative signs and dates the initial license application and each renewal application. Another person may not sign in that role.

The Authorized CILA Agency Representative keeps a current organizational chart that shows reporting lines from the governing body through the Authorized CILA Agency Representative to the site managers and direct support staff (DSPs). The chart is revised within 10 business days of any change in structure or key personnel.

The Authorized CILA Agency Representative keeps a current staffing pattern and written staff qualifications for each position. These are the same documents submitted with the license application. They are updated whenever a position changes or a site is added.

Before opening a site and at each Personal Plan review, the Authorized CILA Agency Representative or designee sets the staffing pattern for the site from the Personal Plans and Implementation Strategies of the people who live there. The basis for the pattern is written in the site staffing file. The agency does not use a fixed ratio as a substitute for individual need.
The agency does not admit more than 8 individuals to any one CILA site. The Authorized CILA Agency Representative confirms capacity in writing before each admission is approved.

The agency provides at least two ways for individuals, guardians and representatives to give input to the governing body. These are (a) an annual written input survey, and (b) an open invitation to submit comments to the Board Chair at [ADDRESS] or [PHONE] at any time. Input is delivered to the governing body at its next regular meeting.

The governing body reviews all input received at the next meeting and records in the minutes what it decided and why. The Authorized CILA Agency Representative tells the person who gave the input, in a format they can understand, what action was taken.
The Authorized CILA Agency Representative reports to the governing body at each meeting on staffing, critical incidents, finances, licensure status, survey results and open corrective actions.
The governing body reviews the performance of the Authorized CILA Agency Representative at least annually and records the review.
The governing body reviews the organizational chart, staffing patterns and bylaws annually and records the review date in the minutes.

If the Authorized CILA Agency Representative leaves or is removed, the governing body appoints a successor within 30 calendar days and notifies the Bureau of Accreditation, Licensure and Certification (BALC) and the Division of Developmental Disabilities (DDD) in writing.

responsibilities.duty: Holds authority over the agency, appoints and evaluates the Authorized CILA Agency Representative, approves policies, and reviews input from individuals, guardians and representatives.
Carries overall fiscal and programmatic responsibility, signs license applications, keeps the organizational chart and staffing patterns current, and reports to the governing body.
Conducts meetings, keeps minutes, and receives input from individuals, guardians and representatives.
Carry out the staffing pattern set from each person's Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy and report staffing problems to the Authorized CILA Agency Representative.

documentation: Bylaws or governing document
Governing body meeting minutes
Resolution appointing the Authorized CILA Agency Representative
Current organizational chart with revision dates
Staffing patterns and staff qualifications for each position
Site staffing basis memos tied to Personal Plans and Implementation Strategies
Individual, guardian and representative input log and the governing body's responses
Annual evaluation of the Authorized CILA Agency Representative

policies.title: Licensure, Site Certification and Provider Agreements (BALC / DDD)
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Authorized CILA Agency Representative, administrators and anyone who handles licensing, site development, enrollment or Medicaid agreements for [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] holds and keeps every license, site certification, enrollment and agreement needed to operate CILA sites lawfully and to be paid under the Medicaid HCBS Waiver for Adults with Developmental Disabilities.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates a CILA only under a license from the IDHS Bureau of Accreditation, Licensure and Certification (BALC) and with each site certified under 210 ILCS 135 and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115. The agency does not admit anyone to a site before BALC has approved it, and does not bill Medicaid before IMPACT enrollment is complete. The agency meets every deadline for applications, renewals, ownership-change notices and operational start-up. Every new site is checked against the siting rules before the agency leases, buys or takes possession of it.

definitions.definition: The IDHS Bureau of Accreditation, Licensure and Certification, which licenses CILA agencies, certifies sites and conducts renewal and complaint surveys.
The IDHS Division of Developmental Disabilities, the operating agency for the Adults with Developmental Disabilities waiver.
The first license, valid for up to one year, for one site serving up to 8 people.
The Illinois Medicaid enrollment and reimbursement system. Enrollment must be complete before federal reimbursement.
A residence the agency owns or controls. It must meet the HCBS settings requirements in 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4).

procedures: The Authorized CILA Agency Representative keeps a licensing calendar that lists every application, renewal, notification and inspection deadline in this policy. The calendar is reviewed at each governing body meeting.

Before submitting an application, the Authorized CILA Agency Representative checks the new-provider requirements against the one-year completion period that runs from the date the application is requested. The date of the request is recorded.

The agency submits the license application with the nonrefundable fee of $200. The application includes the agency's policies and procedures, organizational chart, staffing patterns and staff qualifications. The Authorized CILA Agency Representative signs and dates it and certifies compliance with 210 ILCS 135/4, Part 115 and the HCBS settings requirements.

Before any lease, purchase or possession of a site, the Authorized CILA Agency Representative checks the site against the siting rules. The site may not be adjacent to, across from, diagonal to or behind another waiver-funded residential or day site of the agency. It may not be in a building that provides inpatient institutional treatment. It may not push Department-funded CILAs owned or controlled by CILA providers above 25% of the units in the building.

If a siting waiver is needed, the Authorized CILA Agency Representative files the waiver request with DDD before leasing, buying or taking possession. The agency does not sign a lease or purchase agreement until it has the written decision.

When the property is ready, the agency gives BALC the documents it needs, including fire clearance information. BALC arranges the request to the Office of the State Fire Marshal. The agency does not admit anyone until BALC has inspected and approved the site. BALC's site inspection runs within 15 working days after it receives the fire clearances and other documents.
The agency completes the electronic fingerprint background check required of owners, authorized representatives, officers or administrator at application, and keeps the results on file.
After receiving BALC's provisional license notice, the agency completes the DDD enrollment steps and IMPACT enrollment. No Medicaid claim is submitted until IMPACT enrollment is confirmed in writing.
The agency confirms that the Medicaid waiver agreement and each person's rate information are on file before the first admission. See GOV-05.

The agency becomes operational within 18 months. If the agency is not operational by that date, the agency understands that the application will be treated as abandoned. The Authorized CILA Agency Representative reports progress against this deadline to the governing body every quarter.

The agency keeps its license, and the BALC site certification for each site, available at the site. It prepares for BALC's unannounced visit, which occurs within one year of the first admission, and for the site visit within six months. Under the current process, a passing agency is moved from a provisional to a permanent license for 3 years. HB5471 would shorten the term. Its status is unverified, so the Authorized CILA Agency Representative checks the current license term with BALC at each renewal.

The agency submits its renewal application at least 120 days before the license expires after Department notice. The Authorized CILA Agency Representative sets internal due dates at least 150 days before expiration to allow for review.
The agency notifies BALC and DDD in writing of any ownership change within 60 business days. The Authorized CILA Agency Representative sends the notice and keeps proof of delivery.
When BALC issues survey findings, the Authorized CILA Agency Representative sends a plan of correction by the date BALC sets and tracks each item to completion. See GOV-04.

The Authorized CILA Agency Representative contacts BALC at 312-814-5310 or DHS.BALC@illinois.gov, or at 401 S. Clinton, 7th Floor, Chicago, IL 60607. The email address is confirmed with BALC before first use because two spellings appear in published sources.

responsibilities.duty: Approves license applications, new sites and siting waiver requests, and reviews licensing status quarterly.
Signs applications, keeps the licensing calendar, files notices and waivers, completes enrollment, and manages BALC and DDD communications.
Keeps current licenses and certifications at each site and prepares the site for visits and surveys.
Confirms IMPACT enrollment before any Medicaid claim is submitted.

documentation: License application package and proof of the $200 fee
Licensing calendar
Date the application was requested and operational-deadline tracking
Siting review for each site and any waiver request and decision
Fire clearance and BALC inspection records
Provisional and permanent licenses and site certifications
IMPACT and DDD enrollment confirmations
Ownership-change notices with proof of delivery
BALC survey reports and plans of correction

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
policies.applies_to: The Authorized CILA Agency Representative, administrators, site managers and every person who writes, approves or uses agency policies
policies.purpose: To keep the agency's written policies and procedures current, approved, accurate and in the hands of the staff who use them. The policies are part of the license application and are reviewed by BALC.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a complete Policy and Procedure Manual that reflects the current text of 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115, including the amendments effective 5/31/2023. Policies are approved by the governing body, version-controlled and reviewed on a fixed schedule. The agency does not rely on superseded BALC templates. Admission policies are in writing and available for review. The agency keeps a copy of its restraint policy. The disaster preparedness plan is reviewed at least annually.

definitions.definition: A policy, plan or form that has a version number, an approver, an effective date and a next review date.
A record of every revision, including the approver, the date and the next review date.
The agency's written plan for disasters and public health crises, reviewed annually.

procedures: The Authorized CILA Agency Representative appoints a policy coordinator, who is [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] unless another person is named in writing.
The policy coordinator keeps a master index of all policies by ID and title, with the version number, effective date, approver and next review date.
The policy coordinator keeps a version log. Each entry records the change made, the reason, the person who drafted it, the approver and the date.
New and revised policies are approved by the governing body, and the approval is recorded in the meeting minutes. A policy is not effective, and is not distributed, until approved.

Before the license application is submitted, the governing body approves the full manual. The agency understands that failing BALC's policy review bars reapplying for one calendar year. The policy coordinator therefore checks each policy against the text of Part 115 before submission.

The policy coordinator confirms that every policy reflects Part 115 as amended effective 5/31/2023, including person-centered planning and conflict-free case management. Older BALC templates are not used.

Each policy is reviewed at least annually. The policy coordinator also triggers a review within 30 calendar days after any change in the law or rule, a BALC or DDD notice, a survey finding, a critical incident that exposes a gap, or a request by the governing body.

The agency reviews the disaster preparedness plan at least annually, revises it as needed, and records the review date and the reviewer's name. Corrective actions arising from drill or inspection deficiencies are recorded in the same file.
The agency keeps its admission policies in writing and makes them available on request to BALC, DDD, individuals and guardians.
The agency keeps a current copy of its restraint policy, consistent with 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.245, in the policy manual and at each site.

The policy coordinator distributes each approved or revised policy to site managers within 5 business days. Site managers train staff on the change before the staff are expected to follow it and have each staff member sign a training acknowledgment.
The policy coordinator removes superseded versions from site binders and electronic folders, keeps one archived copy of each earlier version, and records the removal in the version log.
Policies are kept at each site and are available to staff, individuals and guardians at all times. Individuals receive information about policies that affect them in a format they can understand.
The policy coordinator reports at least annually to the governing body on completed reviews, overdue reviews and pending changes.

responsibilities.duty: Approves new and revised policies and receives the annual review report.
Ensures policies match current rules and are applied in practice.
Maintains the master index and version log, schedules reviews and distributes policies.
Keep current policies at the site, train staff and return signed acknowledgments.

documentation: Policy and Procedure Manual with master index
Version log
Governing body approval minutes
Annual review records
Staff training acknowledgments
Disaster preparedness plan with annual review record
Written admission policies
Restraint policy
Archive of superseded versions

policies.title: Quality Improvement, Data Review and Mortality Review
policies.applies_to: The governing body, Authorized CILA Agency Representative, administrators, nurses, site managers and the Behavior Management/Human Rights Committee
policies.purpose: To make [AGENCY NAME] review how it is performing, find problems early, correct them, and learn from critical incidents and deaths.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] runs a standing quality improvement program. It reviews data on health, safety, rights and service delivery at least quarterly, follows the monitoring and evaluation requirements of Part 115, and tracks each corrective action to closure. Every death receives an internal mortality review. Part 115 does not set a mortality-review procedure, so this process is agency practice. Restraint use and behavior modifications are referred to the Behavior Management/Human Rights Committee.

definitions.definition: An event defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120 that must be reported, including deaths. Incidents are entered in the Critical Incident Reporting and Analysis System (CIRAS).
As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120 and regulated by 115.245.
An internal review of the circumstances, care and any contributing factors surrounding a death, done to identify preventable risks.
A specific step, with an owner and a due date, taken to fix a problem found by review, survey or inspection.

procedures: The Authorized CILA Agency Representative appoints a quality improvement lead, who is [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] unless another person is named in writing. The lead convenes a quality review at least quarterly.
Before each quarterly review, site managers and the nurse send the lead the data listed in step 3 for their sites, by the 10th day after the end of the quarter.

At each quarterly review, the team examines at least the following: critical incidents, including CIRAS entries; injuries; peer-to-peer aggression; restraint use; unscheduled hospitalizations; missing-person events; rights complaints and grievances; and BALC and other survey findings.
The team looks for patterns by individual, site, shift, staff member, time of day and type of event, and records its findings in the quality review minutes.
For each problem found, the team writes a corrective action that names the responsible person and a due date, and records it in the corrective action log.

The lead tracks each corrective action to completion. An action is closed only when the lead has verified in writing that the problem is fixed. Overdue actions are reported to the Authorized CILA Agency Representative within 5 business days after the due date.
The agency keeps records of how deficiencies from surveys and inspections were corrected and has them available for BALC and DDD.

Every use of restraint is referred to the Behavior Management/Human Rights Committee, as is every behavior modification. The committee records its review and any recommendation. Prone, supine and mechanical restraint are prohibited and any use is reported in CIRAS and to the Office of the Inspector General.
When an individual dies, the Authorized CILA Agency Representative opens a mortality review within 7 calendar days. The review is separate from, and does not delay, the reports required by HW-05.

The mortality review looks at the person's health history and recent changes, medication records, health monitoring, response to any change of condition, emergency actions, staff training and any other relevant facts. It records the findings and any contributing factors that could be prevented.

The review team completes the written mortality review within 60 calendar days, or documents why more time is needed. The review is presented to the governing body at its next meeting. Any resulting corrective action is entered in the corrective action log.

Information from reviews is shared with the people who live at the site and their guardians only as allowed by IR-04, and staff are given the lessons learned without identifying information that is not needed for their work.

The lead writes an annual quality improvement summary covering trends, actions closed, actions open and the results of any changes made. The governing body reviews the summary and records its response in the minutes.
Quality review records are kept for the retention period set in the agency's record retention schedule and are available to BALC and DDD on request.

responsibilities.duty: Reviews the annual summary and the mortality review reports, and requires corrective action.
Ensures the program runs, resources are provided and overdue actions are resolved.
Convenes reviews, analyzes data, maintains the corrective action log and verifies closure.
Provides health data and takes part in mortality reviews.
Submit complete data and carry out assigned corrective actions.
Reviews restraint use and behavior modifications and records its recommendations.

documentation: Quarterly quality review minutes and data summaries
Corrective action log with closure verification
Critical incident and CIRAS records
Records of how survey and inspection deficiencies were corrected
Behavior Management/Human Rights Committee referrals and minutes
Mortality review reports
Annual quality improvement summary and governing body response

policies.title: Medicaid Compliance, Billing and Service Documentation
policies.applies_to: The Authorized CILA Agency Representative, billing and compliance staff, site managers, nurses and direct support staff who document services
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] bills Medicaid only for services that are authorized, delivered and documented, and that it meets Medicaid enrollment, rate, wage pass-through and electronic visit verification requirements.
policies.policy: CILA services are paid under the Medicaid HCBS Waiver for Adults with Developmental Disabilities (IL.0350.R05.04) through IMPACT. HFS is the Medicaid agency and IDHS-DDD is the operating agency. [AGENCY NAME] bills only for services identified in the individual's Personal Plan, only at the rate set for that individual, and only for days and services supported by documentation. Medicaid does not pay room and board, so residents pay it from their own income, such as SSI. The agency does not bill day program services within the CILA rate. Day programs are billed separately.

definitions.definition: The program code for 24-hour CILA, including host family.
The program code for intermittent CILA.
Electronic documentation of when and where certain services are delivered. It is required for IMPACT providers billing personal care or home health care.
Certification that DDD wage or rate increases are passed through to direct care staff.
The person-centered plan that identifies the individual's services, including every service the agency bills.

procedures: The agency confirms IMPACT enrollment in writing before submitting any claim. The compliance lead keeps the confirmation on file.
Before each admission, the compliance lead obtains and files the individual's rate letter. Rates are individually determined, so the agency does not assume a standard rate for any person or home.

The agency bills only services identified in the individual's Personal Plan. If a service the individual needs or receives is not in the plan, the site manager tells the individual's Independent Service Coordination (ISC) agency in writing so the plan can be changed. The service is not billed until the plan includes it.
The compliance lead keeps the correct program code for each person (60D or 61H) in the billing record and checks it against the rate letter each month.

Each direct support staff member documents services daily as described in PCS-04. The note shows the date, the service delivered, the Implementation Strategy outcome supported, and the staff member's name and signature or electronic identifier.

Before billing each month, the site manager reviews every individual's documentation against the days to be billed and signs a monthly review sheet. Days without support documentation are not billed. Any gaps are explained in writing.
The compliance lead reconciles each claim to attendance and residence records, including hospital stays, respite and absences, and does not bill for days the individual was not in the service.
The agency does not include day program costs in the CILA claim. If the agency also provides day services, those are documented and billed separately.
The compliance lead asks DDD in writing whether 60D and 61H claims are covered by the EVV requirement, and files the answer. This coverage is unverified until DDD confirms it.

If DDD confirms that EVV applies, the agency enrolls staff in the EVV system, trains them, and reviews EVV compliance monthly. The compliance lead keeps quarterly compliance above 75% from April 1, 2026 and reports it to the Authorized CILA Agency Representative.

For each DDD rate or wage increase that carries a pass-through requirement, the Authorized CILA Agency Representative signs the pass-through certification. The compliance lead keeps payroll records that show the increase reached direct care staff.

The agency does not bill Medicaid for room and board. The site manager, with the individual's agreement, sets up the room-and-board payment from the individual's income as described in IR-05, and records it separately from waiver billing.

The agency meets the HCBS person-centered planning and settings requirements in 42 CFR 441.301(c) and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.200 as conditions of payment. The compliance lead raises any gap with the Authorized CILA Agency Representative immediately.

The compliance lead performs a quarterly internal audit of a sample of each site's records, checking claims against the Personal Plan, rate letter, daily documentation and attendance. Errors are corrected, and overpayments are reported and returned as the Medicaid program requires.
The compliance lead retains billing and service records for the period required by the Medicaid program and the agency's retention schedule, and makes them available to HFS, DDD and BALC on request.

responsibilities.duty: Is accountable for Medicaid compliance and signs wage pass-through certifications.
Maintains enrollment, rate letters, claims, audits and EVV compliance if applicable.
Review daily documentation monthly before billing and notify the ISC of needed plan changes.
Document each service accurately and on time.
Documents nursing oversight and health services delivered to each person.

documentation: IMPACT enrollment confirmation
Individual rate letters
Personal Plan service lists tied to billing
Daily service documentation
Monthly site manager review sheets
Claims and reconciliation records
Written DDD response on EVV coverage and EVV compliance reports if applicable
Wage pass-through certifications and payroll records
Quarterly internal audit reports
Room-and-board payment records, kept separately from waiver billing

policies.title: Agency Closure, Independent Monitors and Receiverships
policies.applies_to: The governing body, Authorized CILA Agency Representative, administrators, site managers and all staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To protect the individuals who live in [AGENCY NAME] sites if the agency closes, loses its license or Medicaid enrollment, or is placed under an Independent Monitor or Receiver, and to set out how the agency will cooperate with those roles.
policies.policy: If [AGENCY NAME] plans to close a site or the agency, or is subject to an Independent Monitor or Receiver, the first priority is the safety, continuity of supports, rights and choices of each individual. The agency gives at least 30 days' notice before a closure and makes adequate transition arrangements for each person. It cooperates fully with any Independent Monitor or Receiver. Records are transferred in a way that protects confidentiality.

definitions.definition: A person who is not Department or State staff, assigned by the Department when the agency operates without a license or the license is suspended, revoked or not renewed. Other triggers include notice to end or not renew the DDD agreement, a closure without adequate transition arrangements at least 30 days beforehand, an emergency threat to health or safety that the agency cannot or will not fix, or termination from Medicaid.
A court-appointed person who takes custody of an unlicensed or sanctioned agency. The Receiver cannot be an owner or an affiliate of the agency.
The steps that move an individual to a new provider or setting of the individual's choice without a gap in supports.

procedures: If the governing body is considering closing the agency or a site, it records the decision in its minutes and appoints the Authorized CILA Agency Representative to lead a written closure plan.

The closure plan names, for each individual, the planned date of closure, the choices available for a new provider or home, the supports needed during the move, the records to be transferred and the staff responsible.

At least 30 days before closure, the agency notifies BALC and DDD in writing. It also notifies the Independent Service Coordination (ISC) agency, each individual and each guardian. Notices to individuals are given in a format and language the person understands.

The agency does not close, and does not discharge anyone, without adequate transition arrangements in place at least 30 days beforehand. If it cannot meet that timeline, the Authorized CILA Agency Representative tells BALC and DDD immediately and asks for help.

Each individual and guardian is told they may choose among available providers and settings, and the agency supports visits and planning. The agency does not steer anyone toward a particular provider. See PCS-08.

The site manager and nurse prepare a transition packet for each person, including the current Personal Plan, Implementation Strategy, health and medication information, risk plans, rights modifications and contact information. The packet is released only with consent or as the law permits.

The agency keeps staffing, supervision and medication administration at the level each Personal Plan requires through the last day of service, and records it. Staff are told of the closure date and of their own responsibilities.

The agency transfers individuals' funds, personal property and records as described in IR-05 and IR-04, with a signed receipt from the individual, guardian or new provider, and protects confidentiality in line with the Confidentiality Act.

If the Department assigns an Independent Monitor, the Authorized CILA Agency Representative gives the monitor access to the sites, individuals, staff and records. The monitor observes operations, advises on compliance and reports to the Department.

The Authorized CILA Agency Representative designates one staff member as the monitor's contact and answers the monitor's requests within the time the monitor sets. The agency does not interfere with the monitor's work or retaliate against anyone who speaks with the monitor.
The agency carries out corrective actions the monitor recommends, or explains in writing to the monitor and BALC why it cannot. The quality improvement lead tracks them to closure. See GOV-04.

If a court appoints a Receiver, the agency follows the court's order and the Receiver's directions. The Receiver cannot be an owner or affiliate of the agency. The agency hands over the records, keys, accounts and information the Receiver needs and keeps a log of what was transferred.
The agency tells individuals and guardians promptly and in plain language about any monitor, receivership or loss of license, how it affects them, and who to contact with questions or concerns.
After closure, the Authorized CILA Agency Representative keeps records that are still required, with a named custodian, and tells BALC and DDD where they are kept.

Section 115.326 text was not retrieved when this policy was drafted. The policy coordinator pulls the text of the Part 115 provisions on Independent Monitors and Receivers and updates this policy before the manual is finalized. See GOV-03.

responsibilities.duty: Decides on closure, approves the closure plan and ensures funds and staff are available through transition.
Leads closure planning, notifies regulators, and is the agency's contact for any monitor or Receiver.
Maintain safe supports through the last day of service and carry out each person's transition steps.
Prepares health and medication information for each person and takes part in handoff to the new provider.
Pulls and reviews the Part 115 text on Independent Monitors and Receivers and updates this policy.

documentation: Governing body minutes recording the closure decision
Written closure plan
Notices to BALC, DDD, ISC agencies, individuals and guardians, with dates
Individual transition plans and choices offered
Transition packets and release records
Receipts for transferred funds, property and records
Log of items handed to a Receiver
Independent Monitor access and corrective action records
Record of the post-closure records custodian

policies.title: Individual Rights and HCBS Settings Requirements
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] CILA sites, all individuals served, guardians, and all staff, contractors and volunteers
policies.purpose: To make sure every person served in a [AGENCY NAME] Community Integrated Living Arrangement (CILA) knows their rights, can use them, and lives in a home that meets the Illinois CILA rule and the federal Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) settings requirements.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] protects the rights of every individual under 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.250 and Chapter II of the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Code. Each CILA site supports community integration, control of personal resources, privacy, dignity and respect, and freedom from coercion and restraint. No site may be an institutional-type setting or have the qualities of one. Because [AGENCY NAME] owns or controls its sites, each site meets 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi)(A)-(E): a written residency agreement with eviction protections, privacy including a lockable bedroom door, individual control of schedule and access to food, visitors at any time, and physical accessibility. Seclusion, time-out and aversive procedures are not permitted. Any limit on a right may be imposed only through IR-02.

definitions.definition: The current Department form listing individual rights, which the agency must share and explain at entry and annually.
The federal conditions in 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4) that a residential setting must meet to be paid under the Medicaid HCBS waiver.
A residence the agency owns, leases or otherwise controls. These sites must meet the added conditions in 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi)(A)-(E).
As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120. It is prohibited in all services and settings.
Practices that are prohibited under 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.250 and are not available to staff under any circumstances.

procedures: At entry, and again every year no later than the anniversary of entry, the QIDP or Program Director gives the current Rights of Individuals form (IL 462-1201) to the individual and the guardian and explains it in the person's preferred language and communication method (see IR-07).

The staff member who explains the form records the date, the person who explained it, who was present, and how the individual showed understanding. The individual and guardian sign the acknowledgment. If the individual declines to sign, staff note this and do not treat it as a refusal of rights.

At entry and annually, staff give each individual and guardian the address and telephone number of the Guardianship and Advocacy Commission (GAC), the Department's Office of the Inspector General (OIG), the Department, and Equip for Equality. The Authorized CILA Agency Representative confirms the current numbers before they are printed or posted: GAC [PHONE], OIG [PHONE], Department/BALC 312-814-5310, Equip for Equality [PHONE].
The Program Director posts the same contact information, in accessible formats, in a common area of every site where individuals can read it without asking staff.

Staff offer to help any individual who wants to contact GAC, Equip for Equality, OIG, the Department or the agency human rights committee, including making the call, writing the message, or arranging private use of a phone or computer. Staff do not screen, delay or ask the reason for these contacts.
Staff tell individuals that they may stay in the CILA unless they voluntarily withdraw or meet the termination criteria in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.215. Any discharge follows PCS-08.

Each individual may choose private physicians and other professionals. The QIDP records each choice in the Personal Plan or Implementation Strategy, and staff arrange transportation and scheduling support for those appointments.

Before admission, the Program Director gives the individual and guardian a written residency agreement. It states the individual's responsibilities, eviction and discharge protections, and the process for challenging a discharge. The agreement may not give the individual less protection than a tenant would have under Illinois landlord-tenant law. Room and board terms follow IR-05.

The Program Director makes sure each individual has a bedroom door that locks, with keys held by the individual and only those staff who need them to respond to an emergency. Individuals may choose their own furnishings and decorate their rooms. Individuals choose their roommates where shared rooms exist, and they may ask to move.

Staff support each individual's choice of daily schedule, including sleep and wake times, meals and activities. Individuals have access to food at any time. Staff do not lock the kitchen or food storage unless a modification approved under IR-02 is in place.
Individuals may have visitors of their choosing at any time, with no set visiting hours. The only limits on visits are those the individual sets, or an approved modification under IR-02.

The Program Director checks each site's physical accessibility, including communal areas, to confirm it fits the needs of the people who live there. Any barrier is reported to the Authorized CILA Agency Representative and fixed or reasonably accommodated.

Staff may not use seclusion, time-out or aversive procedures. Any staff member who sees or suspects one of these, or any other violation of rights, reports it immediately to the Program Director or Authorized CILA Agency Representative. Abuse, neglect, exploitation and restraint are reported under the agency's reporting procedures.

Each month, the QIDP or site supervisor does a rights walkthrough at each site. They check the posted information, locks, food access, visitor practices, privacy and the condition of individuals' belongings, and record the result and any follow-up on the site review log.
The Authorized CILA Agency Representative reviews the site review logs each quarter and reports patterns and corrective actions to the governing body through GOV-04.

The Human Resources Manager includes rights training in orientation and in annual refresher training for all staff. It covers HCBS settings requirements, the Rights of Individuals form, and the prohibition on seclusion, time-out, aversive procedures and coercion.

responsibilities.duty: Makes sure the rights process is followed at every site, confirms the contact numbers for GAC, OIG, the Department and Equip for Equality, and reports rights findings to the governing body.
Explains the rights form at entry and annually, documents private-provider choices in the plan, and does the monthly rights walkthrough.
Keeps each site compliant with the HCBS settings conditions and keeps rights information posted.
Respect individual rights daily, offer help to contact advocacy organizations, and report any rights violation immediately.
Reviews any limit on rights under IR-02 and is available to individuals as a contact.

documentation: Signed acknowledgment of the Rights of Individuals form (IL 462-1201), at entry and each year
Record of the explanation, showing who, when and how understanding was checked
Posted contact information list, with the date the numbers were last confirmed
Residency agreement and room and board agreement for each individual
Private physician and professional choices in the Personal Plan / Implementation Strategy
Monthly site rights walkthrough logs
Rights training records for all staff

policies.title: Rights Restrictions, Modifications and Due Process
policies.applies_to: All individuals served, guardians, the QIDP, the Provider Support Team, the Behavior Management/Human Rights Committee and all direct support staff
policies.purpose: To make sure that no individual's rights are limited except through an individualized, justified, consented and regularly reviewed modification, and that every individual has a real way to challenge it.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] limits an individual's rights or HCBS settings protections only through a modification written into the Personal Plan and the Implementation Strategy. Each modification must be based on an assessed need and must meet the conditions in 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi)(F). The Implementation Strategy states the periods of time and activity restrictions at home and the locations and time frames for community access (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.230). No restriction may be used for staff convenience or because of staffing concerns. Any restrictive behavior support needs approval by the Behavior Management/Human Rights Committee. Seclusion, time-out and aversive procedures are prohibited (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.250). Prone, supine and mechanical restraint are prohibited. Any other restraint is permitted only if every condition in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.245 is met.

definitions.definition: A documented, individualized limit on a right or HCBS settings condition, based on a specific assessed need and recorded in the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy.
As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120. Prone, supine and mechanical restraint are prohibited. Any other restraint may be used only under 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.245.
As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120. These are prohibited.
The team that develops and approves supports with the individual and guardian, including the QIDP and, as needed, the ISC and clinicians.
The committee that reviews and approves restrictive behavior supports and restraint plans.

procedures: Staff may not impose any rule, limit or practice that restricts an individual's rights (for example, access to food, visitors, money, locks, schedule, or time alone or in the community) unless it is an approved modification. A staff member who thinks a limit is needed tells the QIDP the same day and does not apply it on their own.

The QIDP convenes the Provider Support Team, including the individual and guardian, to identify the specific, assessed need that the limit would address. The need must be documented. A general reference to safety or to the diagnosis is not enough.

The team documents the positive interventions and supports already tried and the less intrusive methods tried and why they did not work. A restriction is considered only after these steps are recorded.

The modification is written into the Personal Plan and the Implementation Strategy. It describes the specific limit in proportion to the need, the periods of time and activities it covers at home, and the locations and time frames for community access (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.230).
The Implementation Strategy includes an assurance that the interventions and supports will cause no harm to the individual, and the QIDP records that the team has confirmed this.

The QIDP states in writing that the modification is not for staff convenience and is not caused by staffing levels. Any modification that appears to be driven by staffing is rejected and sent to the Authorized CILA Agency Representative for review.
The team sets a method to collect data on the modification's use and effect, and sets a time frame after which the modification is reviewed, ended or renewed.
Any restrictive behavior support is sent to the Behavior Management/Human Rights Committee before it starts. Use begins only after the committee approves it.

The QIDP explains the proposed modification to the individual and guardian in plain language, including the reason, the alternatives, the data to be collected, and the right to refuse and to contest it. Written informed consent from the individual and guardian is obtained before the modification takes effect and is placed in the record. If consent is refused, the restriction is not started.

Staff do not use seclusion, time-out or aversive procedures. They also do not use prone, supine or mechanical restraint. Any use of one of these is reported immediately to the Authorized CILA Agency Representative, who makes the required reports, including in CIRAS and to the Office of the Inspector General.

Any other restraint may be used only if all conditions are met: there is an immediate threat of serious physical harm and less restrictive measures have been shown to be ineffective; the restraint is a modification in the Personal Plan, approved by the individual or guardian and the Provider Support Team, and included in the behavior strategy; the Behavior Management/Human Rights Committee has approved it along with a plan to reduce and eliminate it; the staff are trained in the specific restraint; and the agency has documented that there is no medical or psychological contraindication (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.245). If any condition is not met, the restraint may not be used.

Staff involved in a restraint that is not in the individual's Personal Plan complete remediation training if the Department requires it. The Authorized CILA Agency Representative keeps a copy of the agency's restraint policy as required by 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.245.

The QIDP reviews every active modification at least monthly with the monthly Implementation Strategy review, using the collected data. The QIDP records whether it is still needed and whether it can be reduced or ended. The full Provider Support Team reviews each modification at least annually and whenever the individual's needs change.

Any individual, guardian or staff member may contest a modification at any time. They may use the grievance process (IR-03), ask the Independent Service Coordinator to convene the team, or contact the Guardianship and Advocacy Commission, Equip for Equality or the Department's Office of the Inspector General. Staff must help on request and may not retaliate.

When the team finds the need no longer exists, or the time frame has ended without a renewal, the QIDP ends the modification the same day, revises the Implementation Strategy, and tells the individual, guardian and all staff who support the person.
The Authorized CILA Agency Representative reports the number and type of active modifications, and any restraint use, to the governing body each quarter through GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Leads the team process, writes the modification, gets informed consent, collects data and reviews the modification at least monthly.
Identifies the need, confirms less intrusive methods were tried, and approves or rejects each modification.
Reviews and approves restrictive behavior supports and restraint plans, and reviews plans to reduce and eliminate them.
Rejects restrictions driven by staffing, makes required reports of restraint, keeps the restraint policy, and informs the governing body.
Apply only approved modifications as written, record the required data, and report any unapproved restriction or prohibited practice.

documentation: Modification written into the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy, stating the assessed need, periods of time and activity restrictions, and community access locations and time frames
Record of positive interventions and less intrusive methods tried
No-harm assurance and statement that the modification is not for staff convenience
Behavior Management/Human Rights Committee approval
Written informed consent from the individual and guardian
Data collection sheets and monthly QIDP review notes
Annual team review minutes
Restraint documentation, CIRAS and OIG reports, training and contraindication records, if any restraint is used
Grievance or contest records and the outcome

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
policies.applies_to: All individuals served, guardians, family members, advocates, and all staff
policies.purpose: To give every individual, guardian and representative a safe, easy and effective way to raise a complaint and have it reviewed, and to feed their views back to the governing body.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] has and uses a process for reporting and handling complaints, as required by 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320. This process is in addition to the agency's process for reporting abuse, neglect and exploitation. Any person may complain orally or in writing, with staff help if wanted, and no one is retaliated against for complaining. Individuals and guardians are given the contact information for the Guardianship and Advocacy Commission, the Department's Office of the Inspector General, the Department and Equip for Equality (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.250). The agency also keeps a way for individuals, guardians and representatives to give input to the governing body (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320).

definitions.definition: Any expression of dissatisfaction about services, staff, the home, rights or the agency, whether or not the person uses the word 'grievance'.
The staff member designated by the Authorized CILA Agency Representative to receive, track and respond to complaints.
Any adverse action, threat or change in treatment because a person made a complaint or helped someone else do so.

procedures: At entry and annually, the QIDP gives each individual and guardian the written grievance procedure, explains it in an accessible format (see IR-07), and gives the contact information for GAC, OIG, the Department and Equip for Equality. The Authorized CILA Agency Representative confirms the current numbers before they are printed or posted.
The Program Director posts the grievance procedure and contact information in a common area of every site and keeps blank grievance forms where individuals can take them without asking.

A complaint may be made orally, in writing, through an advocate, or in any other way the person communicates. Any staff member who receives a complaint accepts it, does not discourage it, and gives it to the Grievance Coordinator within one business day.
Staff must help an individual to file a complaint if asked, including writing it down for the person. The individual may have an advocate, guardian, family member or ISC present.

The Grievance Coordinator records the complaint on the grievance log with the date, complainant, a description of the concern, and the outcome the person wants, and gives the complainant a written or other accessible acknowledgment within two business days.

If the complaint alleges abuse, neglect, exploitation or a critical incident, the Grievance Coordinator immediately notifies the Authorized CILA Agency Representative. The matter is handled under the agency's abuse, neglect and exploitation reporting process, and the guardian is notified within 24 hours of receipt of the allegation (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320). The grievance process is not used to delay that reporting.

For all other complaints, the Grievance Coordinator assigns a reviewer who was not involved in the matter. If the complaint is about the Program Director, the Authorized CILA Agency Representative reviews it. If it is about the Authorized CILA Agency Representative, the governing body chair reviews it.

The reviewer talks to the complainant, reviews records, speaks with involved staff, and tries to resolve the matter. Immediate fixes, such as a broken item or a wrong menu, may be made on the spot and recorded.

[AGENCY NAME] gives a written response, in an accessible format, within 10 business days of receipt. The response states what was found, what will be done and when, and how to appeal. If more time is needed, the Grievance Coordinator tells the complainant why and gives a new date.

If the complainant is not satisfied, they may appeal to the Authorized CILA Agency Representative, who reviews and answers in writing within 10 business days. The complainant may also contact GAC, Equip for Equality, the OIG, the Department or the agency human rights committee at any time, with or without using the agency process.

Staff may not retaliate against anyone for filing or helping with a complaint. Any suspected retaliation is reported to the Authorized CILA Agency Representative and reviewed as a separate complaint, with disciplinary action as appropriate.

Each month the Grievance Coordinator reviews the grievance log for trends, such as repeated issues in one house or with one staff member, and gives a summary to the Authorized CILA Agency Representative.

At least quarterly, the Authorized CILA Agency Representative reports the number, types, outcomes and trends of complaints to the governing body, without identifying individuals unless needed, through GOV-04.

At least annually, the agency collects input from individuals, guardians and representatives, such as through a house meeting, satisfaction survey or invitation to attend part of a governing body meeting, and presents the input to the governing body. The governing body records its response.

responsibilities.duty: Receives complaint summaries and input from individuals and guardians, and acts on trends.
Designates the Grievance Coordinator, decides appeals, and makes sure abuse, neglect and exploitation allegations are handled in the proper process.
Logs, acknowledges and tracks complaints and makes sure written responses go out on time.
Explain the process to individuals and guardians, support filing, and resolve complaints at the site level.
Accept and pass on every complaint, help individuals who ask, and never retaliate.

documentation: Written grievance procedure and signed acknowledgment of receipt by individual and guardian
Grievance log, including date, description, reviewer, response date, outcome and appeal
Written acknowledgments and responses
Monthly trend reviews and quarterly governing body reports
Record of individual, guardian and representative input to the governing body and the response
Posted contact list and the date numbers were last confirmed

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
policies.applies_to: All staff, contractors, volunteers and students with access to information about individuals served, and all [AGENCY NAME] sites, offices and electronic systems
policies.purpose: To protect the confidentiality of every individual's records and communications, respect each person's privacy in their home, and comply with state and federal confidentiality law.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] protects individual records and communications under the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act (740 ILCS 110) and certifies compliance with that Act as required by 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.410. Informed consent for a release of information is obtained under the definition in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120. To the extent [AGENCY NAME] is a covered entity or business associate, it also follows the HIPAA Privacy, Security and Breach Notification Rules; it applies the stricter of the two standards when they differ. Staff may share information about an individual only as the Act permits, with valid consent, or as required by law. Staff respect each person's privacy in the bedroom and bathroom. Electronic monitoring of a bedroom is allowed only as set out in IR-09.

definitions.definition: Any record or communication about an individual's services, health, behavior, finances or identity that is protected by the Mental Health and DD Confidentiality Act.
A signed written consent by the individual or guardian that allows named persons or organizations to receive specified information for a stated purpose and period.
Permission freely given after full disclosure of benefits and liabilities, including consent for releases of information (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120).
A written notice explaining how information may be used and disclosed and what rights the individual has, as described in 45 CFR 164.520.
An unauthorized acquisition, access, use or disclosure of protected health information that compromises its security or privacy, as defined in 45 CFR 164.400-414.

procedures: At entry, the QIDP gives the individual and guardian the written notice of privacy practices, explains it in an accessible format, and records the date and the person's acknowledgment. The notice is posted at each site and available at any time on request.

Staff may release information only with a signed release of information that names the recipient, the information covered, the purpose and the expiration, or as otherwise permitted or required by law. Before any release, the staff member checks the form against the record and asks the QIDP when in doubt.

The QIDP explains each release to the individual and guardian before they sign, including that they may refuse and may revoke consent at any time in writing. Informed consent is documented as defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120.

The Records Custodian enters every release and every disclosure outside of routine treatment, payment and operations in the release log, with date, recipient, information given and staff member. Disclosures are available for review by the individual on request.
Staff access only the information they need to do their jobs. The Authorized CILA Agency Representative sets access levels by role and reviews them when staff change jobs or leave.

Each staff member, contractor and volunteer signs a confidentiality agreement at hire, before any access to records, and repeats it annually. Confidentiality and HIPAA training is part of orientation and annual refresher training.
Paper records are kept in locked storage at the site or office, and only authorized staff have keys. Records that are being used are never left in view of visitors, other residents or the public.

Electronic records, including Personal Plans and Implementation Strategies kept at the residence, are on password-protected and encrypted devices. Each user has a unique login and must log off when finished. Staff do not text, email or post information that identifies individuals except through approved secure systems.

Staff do not discuss individuals in public places or in front of other residents, visitors or people who do not need to know. Names and personal details are not shared with unauthorized people, including on social media. Staff do not photograph or record an individual without that person's or guardian's written consent.

Staff respect each individual's privacy in bedrooms and bathrooms. They knock and wait for permission before entering unless there is an emergency. Personal care is given in private. Mail, phone calls and electronic communication belong to the individual and are not opened or monitored by staff unless an approved modification under IR-02 is in place.

Electronic monitoring of an individual's bedroom is allowed only if all requirements in IR-09 and applicable Illinois law are met. No camera, audio recorder or other monitor may be placed in a bathroom or used in any space without that authorization.

Any staff member who knows or suspects that information has been lost, stolen, misdirected or improperly accessed reports it to the Privacy Officer immediately, and in all cases within one business day.

The Privacy Officer investigates, limits any further harm, and documents a risk assessment of the incident. If a breach of unsecured protected health information is confirmed, [AGENCY NAME] notifies the affected individuals and guardians without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery, and notifies the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and, where 500 or more people are affected, the media, as required by 45 CFR 164.400-414.

The Privacy Officer also decides whether the incident is reportable to the Department. The Authorized CILA Agency Representative makes any report to BALC or the Office of the Inspector General that applies.

The Privacy Officer reviews the release log, access levels and any incidents each quarter and reports to the Authorized CILA Agency Representative and, through GOV-04, to the governing body. Staff who violate this policy are subject to discipline up to termination.

responsibilities.duty: Sets access levels, makes sure records are secured, and makes any required reports.
Maintains the notice of privacy practices, investigates incidents, completes breach risk assessments and breach notices, and runs privacy training.
Controls the records, keeps the release log, and checks releases for validity.
Explains the notice and releases to individuals and guardians and obtains informed consent.
Protect confidentiality, access only what they need, and report suspected breaches immediately.

documentation: Signed acknowledgment of the notice of privacy practices
Signed releases of information, with revocations
Release and disclosure log
Staff confidentiality agreements and training records
Records access list by role
Privacy incident reports, risk assessments and breach notifications
Quarterly privacy reviews

policies.title: Personal Funds, Personal Resources and Property
policies.applies_to: All individuals served, guardians, and all staff and contractors who handle money, benefits or personal property
policies.purpose: To make sure every individual controls their own money and property to the greatest extent possible, that funds are safeguarded and accounted for, and that financial exploitation is prevented and reported.
policies.policy: CILA settings must support each individual's control of personal resources (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.200), which is part of community integration (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120). [AGENCY NAME] holds an individual's funds only when the individual or guardian asks or agrees in writing, or when [AGENCY NAME] has been appointed representative payee. Funds are kept separate for each individual and never mixed with agency funds or those of other individuals. Financial exploitation, as defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code Part 50, is a critical incident (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120) and is reported without exception. Staff may not borrow from, accept gifts from, or enter personal financial dealings with any individual.

definitions.definition: Income, benefits, bank accounts, cash and property that belong to the individual.
As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code Part 50 (incorporated by 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120). Staff must treat any misuse of an individual's funds or property as possible financial exploitation.
A person or organization appointed by the Social Security Administration to receive and manage benefits for an individual.
Mixing the funds of an individual with the funds of the agency, staff or other individuals.
The signed written agreement that sets what the individual pays for housing and food, from the individual's own income.

procedures: At admission and at least annually, the QIDP asks the individual and guardian how the person wants to manage their money, including how much support is wanted, and records the choice in the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy. Supports to learn money skills are included if the individual wants them.

[AGENCY NAME] holds funds only on the written request or agreement of the individual or guardian, or as representative payee. The individual may withdraw that agreement and take back control of their money at any time, unless a court order or approved modification says otherwise.

The Authorized CILA Agency Representative opens a separate account for each individual, titled in the individual's name, or keeps a separate ledger for any cash held. Individual funds are never commingled with agency funds or with the funds of others.
Individuals have access to their own money on request, at reasonable times, without staff questioning the reason. Staff help with withdrawals and record each one the same day.

Every deposit or withdrawal is recorded on the individual's ledger with the date, amount, purpose and staff initials. Receipts are collected for all purchases and attached to the ledger. The individual signs for cash received whenever able.

Cash held at the site is kept in a locked box. Two staff count the cash at each shift change, or at least once each day, and both sign the count. Any discrepancy is reported to the Program Director immediately.

The Program Director or a designee reconciles each individual's ledger and account to the bank statement and cash on hand every month. A person other than the one who handled the funds reviews and signs the reconciliation. The Authorized CILA Agency Representative reviews the reconciliations quarterly.
Individuals and guardians may review the individual's ledger at any time. The agency gives them a statement at least quarterly, or more often if requested.

Each individual signs a written room and board agreement before admission. Medicaid does not pay for room and board, and residents typically pay from income such as SSI. The Authorized CILA Agency Representative confirms with the Department Division of Developmental Disabilities and BALC any charge that is permitted before it is set. Charges may not exceed what is stated in the agreement and may not be raised without written notice to the individual and guardian.

If [AGENCY NAME] is representative payee, the Authorized CILA Agency Representative follows the Social Security Administration's rules for using benefits for the individual's current needs and saving the rest (20 CFR 416.635), keeps records, and submits the required accounting reports (20 CFR 416.665). Benefits are not used for any purpose of the agency.

Staff take an inventory of each individual's personal property at admission, record it, and update it at least every six months and at discharge. The individual or guardian signs the inventory. Items of significant value are photographed with the consent of the individual.

Individuals may keep and use their own belongings and decide who may use them. Staff may not take, use, sell or give away an individual's property. If property is lost or damaged by staff or by agency neglect, [AGENCY NAME] replaces or reimburses the individual at the replacement value.

Staff may not borrow money from, lend money to, buy from or sell to, accept gifts from, or enter any personal financial arrangement with an individual. Staff may not be named in an individual's will or on an account. The only exception is a small token gift of nominal value, which must be reported to the Program Director.

Any staff member who suspects that an individual's funds or property are being misused or taken reports it immediately to the Authorized CILA Agency Representative. The agency treats it as a possible critical incident and reports it as required under 59 Ill. Adm. Code Part 50 and 115.120. The guardian is notified within 24 hours of receipt of an allegation of exploitation (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320).
At discharge, the Program Director returns all funds and property to the individual or guardian within the time required by PCS-08, with a final accounting and signed receipt.

responsibilities.duty: Oversees fund management, opens individual accounts, serves or designates the representative payee function, and reviews reconciliations quarterly.
Makes sure ledgers, cash counts, receipts, inventories and monthly reconciliations are done.
Records each person's money-management choices and supports in the plan, and arranges money-skills support if wanted.
Record every transaction, count cash with a second staff member, and report suspected misuse.
Decide how funds are managed and may review records at any time.

documentation: Written agreement or request for the agency to hold funds, and any withdrawal of it
Individual ledgers with receipts, and bank statements
Shift cash count records with two signatures
Monthly reconciliations with reviewer signature, and quarterly review notes
Quarterly statements given to individuals and guardians
Room and board agreement and written notices of any change
Representative payee records and accountings, if applicable
Property inventories and replacement or reimbursement records
Incident reports for suspected financial exploitation

policies.title: Informed Consent, Guardianship and Decision-Making Support
policies.applies_to: All individuals served, guardians and the QIDP, Program Director, Authorized CILA Agency Representative and all staff involved in admission, planning and consent
policies.purpose: To make sure every decision about an individual's services is made by the right person with full information and without coercion, and that individuals are supported to make their own decisions to the greatest extent possible.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] obtains and documents informed consent to participate in a CILA (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.200) and for each release of information and other service decision requiring consent. Informed consent means permission freely given after full disclosure of benefits and liabilities (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120). The agency presumes that every adult individual can make their own decisions unless a court has ruled otherwise. Where a court has appointed a plenary or limited guardian, the guardian decides only within the authority of the order. Coercion is prohibited (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120). No individual who meets the eligibility criteria is refused a placement solely because of diagnosis (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.210). [AGENCY NAME] supports individuals to take part in and make decisions throughout the planning process and under 42 CFR 441.301(c)(1).

definitions.definition: Permission freely given after full disclosure of benefits and liabilities, including consent for releases of information (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120).
A court-appointed plenary or limited guardian. A limited guardian has authority only over the matters named in the court order (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120).
As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120. It includes pressuring or threatening an individual to obtain agreement or compliance, and it invalidates consent.
Help that lets a person understand choices and express a decision, such as plain language, visuals, extra time, a trusted person present, or a communication device.

procedures: Before admission, the QIDP or Program Director asks for a copy of any guardianship order and reads it to confirm whether the guardian is plenary or limited, what authority is given, and any expiration or review date. A copy goes into the record. If there is no guardian, the individual makes their own decisions.

The QIDP records in the record, for each area of decision (residence, health care, finances, releases of information, rights modifications, and other areas), whether the individual, the guardian or both decide. For a limited guardian, the individual decides every matter outside the order.

Before asking anyone to consent, staff explain the choice in plain language and in the person's preferred communication method (see IR-07). The explanation covers what is proposed, why, the benefits and risks, the alternatives, and the right to say no or change one's mind. Staff allow enough time and offer to have a trusted person attend.

Before admission, the QIDP gets and documents written informed consent to participate in the CILA from the individual and the guardian where there is one. The QIDP records how the explanation was given and how the person showed understanding. If the individual does not agree with a guardian's decision, the QIDP records it, explains to the individual how to contest it, and offers help to contact GAC or Equip for Equality.

For a person aged 17½ who is admitted under an age waiver, as permitted by 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.210, the QIDP obtains the consent of the parent or legal guardian along with the individual's agreement, and notes the waiver in the record.

Consent may not be obtained by pressure, threat, promise of a benefit, withholding of services, or any other form of coercion. Staff who witness or suspect coercion report it at once to the Authorized CILA Agency Representative. Consent that was obtained through coercion is void and must be obtained again properly.

Staff do not refuse admission or services solely because of an individual's diagnosis. An agency's limited capacity for a particular disability is not grounds for finding an individual ineligible. Admission decisions follow PCS-01.

Each release of information is explained and signed under IR-04, naming the recipient, content, purpose and expiration. Consent for rights modifications is obtained under IR-02. Consent for medications, treatment and health procedures is obtained under HW-01 and HW-02.

The QIDP obtains consent again when the Personal Plan or Implementation Strategy changes in a way that affects the person, when a release expires, and at least annually. Staff must also seek renewed consent when circumstances change and the earlier consent no longer fits.

Staff and the QIDP support decision-making in daily life and in planning. They offer real choices about daily routines, meals, activities, friends and goals, record the individual's own words and preferences in the plan, and follow those choices unless an approved modification applies.

The QIDP asks the individual in planning meetings how much help they want to make decisions and whom they want involved. The individual's preferences are respected even when a guardian makes the final decision, and the guardian is invited to take the individual's views into account.
A guardian is not permitted to serve as the individual's host family caregiver. The Authorized CILA Agency Representative makes sure this is checked before any host family arrangement is approved.

If the individual's ability to make decisions appears to change, or a guardian appears to be acting against the individual's interests or has become unavailable, the QIDP informs the Authorized CILA Agency Representative. The agency may refer the person to the Guardianship and Advocacy Commission or the Independent Service Coordinator and does not decide on its own that a person lacks capacity.

The QIDP checks each record at least annually to confirm that the guardianship order on file is current, that consents are in date, and that each consent matches who has authority to give it. The Program Director corrects any gaps within 10 business days.

Verifies guardian authority, obtains and documents informed consent, and supports the individual in planning and decision-making.
