policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Communication Access
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] staff, contractors and volunteers involved in referral, admission, service delivery, communication and site management for the Community Integrated Living Arrangement (CILA) program
policies.purpose: To make sure no person is excluded from, denied, or treated differently in CILA services because of diagnosis, disability type, race, color, national origin, language, sex, religion or other discriminatory factors. To make sure every individual can understand and take part in their services through accessible communication and a physically accessible home.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] admits and serves individuals based only on eligibility under the CILA rules, the person's assessed needs, and the capacity of the home. No otherwise qualified individual is denied placement solely on diagnosis. Lack of agency capacity for a particular disability does not make a person ineligible. The agency first considers reasonable accommodations and additional supports. Communal areas of each home meet ADA standards, and a site must be able to serve a wheelchair or mobility device user before it is offered to that person. Interpreters, translated rights materials and accessible formats are provided at no cost to the individual or guardian. Requests for reasonable accommodation are logged and answered in writing. Individuals are not retaliated against for requesting an accommodation or making a complaint.

definitions.definition: A person who is at least 18 (or at least 17.5 with an approved age waiver), has a developmental disability, and needs CILA services and a supervised living arrangement.

A change in a rule, practice, service, communication method or physical feature that lets a person with a disability take part equally in services, unless it would fundamentally alter the service or impose an undue burden.
Information provided in a form the person can use, such as large print, plain language, pictures, audio, Braille, captioned or signed video, or electronic text.
Communication with the individual that is as effective as communication with others, using the person's preferred language, method and aids.

procedures: The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], is the agency's nondiscrimination and accessibility coordinator. The coordinator's name and [PHONE] are posted in each home and included in the admission packet.

Written admission criteria are kept at the agency office and available for review by individuals, guardians, ISC agencies, the Department and BALC. The criteria list only CILA eligibility and capacity factors and no discriminatory factors.

At referral, the Administrator and QIDP review the person's age, developmental disability, need for CILA services and need for a supervised living arrangement. They do not screen out a person by diagnosis, disability type, behavior history labels, race, national origin, language, sex, religion or funding source beyond the waiver requirements.

If the agency believes it lacks capacity for a person's disability, the Administrator documents what supports, training, equipment, staffing or home modifications would be needed. The agency then considers whether these can be provided, including through a request for additional supports under PCS-03, before deciding on the referral.

Every admission decision is recorded on the referral decision record. The record lists the person's needs, the home's capacity, the accommodations considered, and the reasons for the decision. The Administrator signs and dates it.

Before placement is offered to a person who uses a wheelchair or other mobility device, the Administrator or designee confirms the specific site has an accessible entrance, accessible communal areas, a usable bathroom, a bedroom the person can enter and move in, and an evacuation route the person can use. The check is documented on the site accessibility checklist.

If a site cannot serve the person, the agency does not place the person there. The agency offers a suitable accessible home if one is available, or tells the person, guardian and ISC in writing that the agency lacks a suitable home at this time. The notice explains how to contact the ISC agency, the agency grievance process (IR-03), and BALC.

At referral and again at admission, the QIDP identifies each person's communication needs: primary language, hearing, vision, speech, literacy, preferred communication method and assistive devices. These are recorded in the record and addressed in the Implementation Strategy.

The agency arranges a qualified interpreter (spoken or sign language) for the individual or guardian when needed, at no charge. Staff do not require the person to bring their own interpreter and do not rely on family members, other residents or untrained staff to interpret unless the person specifically requests it. The request is documented.

The Rights of Individuals form (IL 462-1201), the grievance procedure, the residency agreement and consent forms are provided in the person's language and in an accessible format. The QIDP explains them in a way the person understands and records the format used and the method of explanation.

Any person, guardian, staff member or ISC may request a reasonable accommodation orally or in writing. The staff member who receives it enters it in the accommodation request log the same business day, noting the date, the requester, the request and the person receiving it.

The coordinator responds to each accommodation request in writing within 10 calendar days, or sooner if the request affects health, safety, communication of an emergency, or a pending decision. The response states whether the request is granted, the date it will be in place, or the reason it is denied and what alternative was offered.

A denied request is reviewed by the Administrator and the individual's team. The individual or guardian is told in writing how to file a grievance under IR-03 and that they may also contact BALC at 312-814-5310 or the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office for Civil Rights.

Staff are trained on this policy, ADA and communication access at hire and annually. The training covers how to use interpreter services, how to log an accommodation request, and how to recognize discriminatory treatment. Training attendance is recorded in the personnel file.

Retaliation, intimidation, or reduced services against anyone who requests an accommodation or makes a discrimination complaint is prohibited. Alleged retaliation is investigated by the Administrator under IR-03.

The Administrator reviews the accommodation log, referral decision records and communication access needs at least annually and reports findings to the governing body through the quality improvement process (GOV-04).

Use each person's preferred communication method, report accommodation requests the same day, and report discrimination concerns.

policies.title: Sexual Health, Relationships and Consent
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] CILA staff, including QIDPs, nurses and Direct Support Professionals, and the Provider Support Team for each individual
policies.purpose: To support each individual's right to sexual health, healthy relationships and healthy sexual practices, and to protect each individual from sexual exploitation and abuse, with respect for privacy, dignity and informed choice.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] supports each individual's right to sexual health and healthy sexual practices and to be free from sexual exploitation and abuse. Provider Support Teams assess the individual's decision-making capacity to consent to sexual activity and plan supports based on that assessment. Staff respect privacy, provide education suited to the person's understanding, and set professional boundaries. The agency does not use coercion or punishment related to a person's sexuality or relationships. Supports are written into the Implementation Strategy. All allegations of sexual abuse or exploitation are reported and investigated through the agency's abuse, neglect and exploitation procedures (BSP-03 and BSP-04).

definitions.definition: A state of physical, emotional and social well-being related to sexuality, including relationships, intimacy, education, protection from infection and unwanted pregnancy, and freedom from coercion and abuse.

definitions.term: Decision-making capacity to consent to sexual activity
definitions.definition: The person's ability to understand the nature of the activity, its risks and consequences, and to voluntarily choose to take part or to refuse.
Any sexual contact or conduct with a person who cannot or does not freely consent, or that takes advantage of power, trust, dependence or the person's disability.
The team made up of the QIDP, a DSP and, as needed, a nurse or other professionals, who plan and provide supports with the individual and guardian.

procedures: At admission and at least annually, the QIDP talks with the individual, and with the guardian as appropriate, about the person's interests, relationships, education needs and preferences concerning sexual health. The conversation is private and in a manner the person understands. Staff record that it took place and the person's stated wishes.

The Provider Support Team assesses the individual's decision-making capacity to consent to sexual activity when there is an expressed interest, an existing relationship, a concern about exploitation, or a change in circumstances. The QIDP organizes the assessment, and a qualified professional participates as needed.

The capacity assessment looks at whether the person understands what is involved, the right to say no, the risks (including infection and pregnancy), and the ability to recognize and report coercion or unwanted contact. It is based on the person's own understanding, with supports such as plain language, pictures or repeated discussions.

The team records the assessment results and any supports needed in the Implementation Strategy. The agency does not conclude that a person lacks capacity because of diagnosis, age or guardianship alone.

The QIDP offers education and supports at the person's level of understanding, such as healthy relationships, consent, personal safety, privacy, reproductive health and prevention of infections. The agency arranges for the nurse, the person's physician or an outside educator to deliver the education when needed.

Staff support the person's right to privacy for personal care, relationships and visits. Staff knock and wait for permission before entering bedrooms and bathrooms except in an emergency, and they do not discuss a person's sexuality or relationships with persons who have no need to know.

Individuals have access to health care for sexual and reproductive health, including private physicians and professionals of their choice. The nurse and QIDP help arrange appointments and transportation when asked, and information is shared only with consent and as the person or guardian authorizes.
Staff do not engage in sexual or romantic relationships with individuals, give gifts of a personal nature, or cross professional boundaries. Staff are trained on this boundary at hire and annually.

When staff observe or learn of behavior that may be sexual exploitation or abuse, they ensure the individual's immediate safety, separate the persons involved, obtain medical care when needed, preserve evidence, and report immediately as required by the agency's abuse, neglect and exploitation procedures (BSP-03 and BSP-04).

Concerns about a person's sexual behavior that raise safety questions for the person or others are brought to the Provider Support Team, which develops positive, non-punitive supports. Any limit on a person's right is handled only through the rights restriction process in IR-02, and never as a matter of staff preference.
The QIDP reviews supports related to sexual health at least monthly as part of the Implementation Strategy review, and updates them when the person's wishes, relationships or capacity change.

Records about sexual health, capacity assessments and relationships are kept confidential under IR-04. They are shared only with the person's team members who need them, and with the guardian and others as the law and the person's consent allow.
The Administrator reviews this policy annually and reports aggregate, de-identified data on education delivered and incident reports to the quality improvement process (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensure this policy is implemented, staff are trained, and allegations are reported and investigated.
Convene the capacity assessment, document supports in the Implementation Strategy, and review them monthly.
Provide health education and coordinate sexual and reproductive health care.
Respect privacy, follow the Implementation Strategy, maintain boundaries, and report concerns immediately.

documentation: Annual sexual health discussion note
Decision-making capacity assessment and team determination
Implementation Strategy entries on supports and education
Education session records
Incident and abuse/neglect reports (as applicable)
Staff training attendance on boundaries and this policy

policies.title: Authorized Electronic Monitoring in Individual Bedrooms
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] CILA staff, the Administrator, and the Provider Support Team for any individual whose bedroom has, or may have, an electronic monitoring device
policies.purpose: To protect the privacy and dignity of individuals in their bedrooms while allowing authorized electronic monitoring only as permitted by the Authorized Electronic Monitoring in Community-Integrated Living Arrangements and Developmental Disability Facilities Act (210 ILCS 165).
policies.policy: Authorized electronic monitoring is the placement of a monitoring device in an individual's room under the Authorized Electronic Monitoring in Community-Integrated Living Arrangements and Developmental Disability Facilities Act (210 ILCS 165). [AGENCY NAME] allows monitoring in an individual's bedroom only when it is requested and authorized as the Act requires, with the notice, consent, roommate consent and posting steps that the Act requires. The agency does not install or use cameras, audio or video recording or other monitoring in bedrooms or bathrooms on its own initiative or outside the Act. Monitoring is never a substitute for required staffing, supervision or supports. Recordings and footage are confidential record information.

definitions.definition: Placement of an electronic monitoring device in an individual's room under 210 ILCS 165, as defined in the CILA rules.
A video, audio or other electronic device as defined by 210 ILCS 165 and used for authorized monitoring.
The person with authority under the Act to ask for monitoring in an individual's room, such as the individual or guardian, as the Act provides.
Any video, audio or other data recorded or transmitted by a monitoring device.

procedures: No monitoring device is placed in any individual's bedroom until the Administrator confirms that the request meets every requirement of 210 ILCS 165. The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], reviews the current text of the Act and the Department's current forms before handling the first request and at least annually thereafter.

A staff member who receives an oral or written request for monitoring in a bedroom gives it to the Administrator the same business day. The Administrator logs the date, the requestor and the individual concerned.

The Administrator identifies who is permitted to make a request under the Act and confirms that the person asking has that authority. The agency does not pressure or encourage any individual, guardian or family member to request or refuse monitoring.

The QIDP meets with the individual, and the guardian if there is one, to explain what monitoring is, where the device would go, who can see or hear the footage, and the right to refuse or withdraw. The explanation is in a format and language the person understands (IR-07).

Written consent and notice documents required by the Act are completed before installation. The individual's own consent is sought and respected to the extent the Act provides, and the guardian's role is handled under IR-06.

When the person shares a bedroom, the roommate's consent, or the consent of the roommate's guardian, is obtained as the Act requires before any device is installed. If consent is not given, or is withdrawn, the device is not used, and the agency discusses other options with the requestor, such as a room change if the individual wishes.

The Administrator confirms that any notice or posting required by the Act is in place at the entrance to the room or other location the Act requires. The agency does not install any device until the posting requirement is met.
The device is placed and used only as the Act and the signed authorization allow. Cameras, audio or recording devices are never placed in bathrooms, and staff do not use hidden devices.

Staff are told that monitoring does not change staffing or supervision. Required on-site support and checks stay in place as written in the Implementation Strategy, and no staff are removed from, or not assigned to, the home because of monitoring.
The QIDP records the monitoring arrangement in the Implementation Strategy, including who requested it, who consented, the room, the date it started, and the reason given, if any.

Footage is treated as confidential under IR-04. Only persons permitted by the Act, the authorization and the agency's confidentiality procedures may view, copy or receive it. The Administrator keeps a log of each time footage is accessed or released, including who, when and why.

Footage that shows possible abuse, neglect or exploitation is preserved and reported under the agency's abuse and neglect reporting procedures (BSP-03 and BSP-04). The Administrator does not delete or alter it.

The individual or other authorized person may withdraw consent or ask for the device to be removed at any time as the Act allows. Staff remove or disable the device promptly once the Administrator confirms the request, and document the date.
The QIDP reviews the need for and the person's continued wishes about monitoring at the monthly Implementation Strategy review and at the annual plan meeting.

Any device found in a bedroom or bathroom that is not authorized is reported immediately to the Administrator, disabled, and investigated. The agency reports as required by law and its incident procedures.
The Administrator reviews all monitoring authorizations, access logs and complaints annually and reports to the governing body through GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Verify that each request meets 210 ILCS 165, keep the monitoring log and access log, ensure posting and consents, and protect footage.
Explain monitoring to the individual, document it in the Implementation Strategy, and review it at least monthly.
Pass requests to the Administrator, never install or move devices on their own, maintain required supervision, and report unauthorized devices or concerning footage.
Review annual monitoring data and ensure the agency does not use monitoring outside the Act.

Written consent, notice and authorization documents required by the Act

Footage access and release log

policies.title: Referral, Admission and Transition In
policies.applies_to: [AGENCY NAME] Administrator, QIDP, nurse, Direct Support Professionals and any staff who handle referrals, admissions, move-ins or residency agreements
policies.purpose: To admit individuals fairly and safely, using the CILA eligibility criteria, the ISC referral process, informed choice, and a planned transition that protects the person's rights and meets HCBS settings requirements.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] admits individuals who are at least 18 with a developmental disability and a need for CILA services and a supervised living arrangement. An age waiver may be requested for a person at least 17.5 and under 18. No otherwise qualified person is denied placement solely on diagnosis. Written admission policies are available for review. Referrals come through the Independent Service Coordination (ISC) agency. The ISC completes Discovery and the Personal Plan within 30 calendar days after waiver services start, and [AGENCY NAME] returns the provider signature page to the ISC within 10 calendar days of receiving the Personal Plan. The individual or guardian takes an active part in choosing the CILA and a home from those available to the general public. Before offering placement the agency confirms that the site is certified, accessible and meets setting rules. At entry the agency obtains written informed consent, the person's service history and the Personal Plan, explains the Rights form (IL 462-1201), and offers a residency agreement for provider-owned or controlled sites. The agency obtains the individual's rate letter before accepting an admission. New individuals are trained on emergency procedures within 30 days of moving in.

definitions.definition: The Independent Service Coordination agency that enrolls people in PUNS, helps them choose services, and develops the Personal Plan.
The person-centered plan developed by the ISC with the individual and guardian, from which the provider's Implementation Strategy is developed.
The ISC's person-centered process for learning about the person's goals, preferences and needs, which leads to the Personal Plan.
Agreement given voluntarily, after the person or guardian has received and understood information about the service, its risks and alternatives, with no coercion.
The Department's notice of the individual's approved CILA rate, which sets the funded supports.
An admission for a person in crisis, such as homelessness, abuse or neglect, handled through the ISC crisis transition process.

procedures: The Administrator keeps the written admission policy at the agency office, makes it available for review on request, and shares it with ISC agencies. It states the eligibility criteria and does not exclude people solely on diagnosis (IR-07).

The Administrator logs each referral from an ISC agency: date, person, ISC contact, and the person's stated preferences. The agency does not accept referrals that bypass the ISC process, except as the ISC crisis process provides.

The Administrator and QIDP review the referral packet and confirm the person is at least 18 with a developmental disability and a need for CILA services and a supervised living arrangement. For a person who is at least 17.5 and under 18, the Administrator requests an age waiver from the Department before admission and does not admit until it is approved.

The QIDP and Administrator meet with the person and guardian (and ISC representative) to learn about the person's goals, preferences, communication, health, behavioral and support needs. The person, guardian and ISC are invited to visit the home and meet housemates and staff.

The Administrator reviews whether the agency has capacity to meet the person's needs, including accessibility, staffing and nursing. The decision is documented with reasons under IR-07. Where more supports are needed, the team may request them under PCS-03 before a decision is made.

The individual or guardian chooses the CILA and a home from those available to the general public. The agency gives accurate information on the available homes, does not steer or limit the choice, and records the choice and the options offered.

Before offering a specific home, the Administrator confirms the site is certified, that communal areas and the person's bedroom, bathroom and routes are accessible for that person's needs, and that the site meets the HCBS settings and siting requirements. The check is documented (GOV-02, IR-07).

The agency obtains the individual's rate letter and confirms the funded supports fit the person's needs before accepting the admission. If the rate does not fit, the QIDP tells the ISC and the team may seek additional supports under PCS-03.

For a person in crisis (homelessness, abuse or neglect), the agency works with the ISC, which submits the Crisis Transition Plan and Funding Request. The agency accepts the person only after confirming the site, staffing and funding are in place, and completes all entry steps in this policy as soon as possible after the move.

The ISC has 30 calendar days after waiver services begin to complete Discovery and the Personal Plan. The Administrator tracks this date, and the QIDP follows up with the ISC if the Personal Plan is late.

Within 10 calendar days after receiving the Personal Plan, the QIDP reviews it, signs and dates the provider signature page and returns it to the ISC. The date of the QIDP's signature starts the 20-day timeline for the Implementation Strategy in PCS-02.

At or before entry, the QIDP obtains written informed consent to participate in the CILA from the individual and guardian, explains the services in a form the person understands, and obtains the person's prior service history, the Personal Plan, guardianship papers, health information and any records required by Part 115 for the record.

At entry the QIDP shares and explains the current Rights of Individuals form (IL 462-1201) with the individual and guardian, gives each person the address and telephone number of the Guardianship and Advocacy Commission, the Department's Office of Inspector General, the Department and Equip for Equality, and documents that the rights were explained. Rights are repeated at least annually (IR-01).

For provider-owned or controlled sites, the Administrator offers a residency agreement that gives the person a legally enforceable right to the home, with protections against eviction comparable to those in landlord-tenant law. The individual or guardian receives a copy and the explanation is documented.

On the move-in day, the QIDP and staff go over house routines, privacy, key or lock access to the bedroom, visitors, personal funds (IR-05), medications (HW-01), and who to call. The nurse completes the entry health review under HW-02.

Within 30 days of the person's move-in, staff train the individual on how to react to fire, severe weather, missing persons, medical and psychiatric emergencies, poison control and death, and the person takes part in an evacuation drill. The training is documented in the individual's record and the site drill record (PCS-04).

The Administrator confirms that all entry items are complete using an admission checklist, signs and dates it, and files it in the record. Items that are late are given a due date and tracked until complete.

Coordinate with the ISC, sign and return the provider signature page within 10 calendar days, obtain consent, explain rights, and manage the transition.
Complete the entry health review and communicate health needs to the team.
Welcome the person, carry out the orientation and emergency training, and support the person's choices during the transition.
Complete Discovery and the Personal Plan within 30 calendar days after services begin and submit the crisis transition plan where applicable.

policies.title: Person-Centered Planning, Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy
policies.applies_to: [AGENCY NAME] QIDPs, Provider Support Teams, nurses, Direct Support Professionals and the Administrator
policies.purpose: To make sure each individual's services are directed by the person's own goals and preferences, as set out in the Personal Plan developed by the ISC and carried out through the agency's Implementation Strategy, within required timelines.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] follows the person-centered planning requirements of 42 CFR 441.301(c)(1)-(3) and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 120. The ISC develops the Personal Plan. The agency's QIDP signs the provider signature page, and the agency develops the Implementation Strategy on Form IL462-4470 within 20 calendar days of the QIDP's dated signature. The strategy covers only the Personal Plan areas the agency agreed to support, is signed by the individual and guardian, and is given to the individual, the guardian and the ISC. It becomes part of the record, and current copies are kept at the residence. The QIDP reviews the strategy at least monthly and documents the review. The strategy is updated at least annually, on any change of status, or on the request of the individual or guardian. The agency bills only for services identified in the Personal Plan.

definitions.definition: The plan developed by the ISC with the individual and guardian that states the person's goals, preferences, needs and chosen services.
The agency's written plan on Form IL462-4470 describing how it will support the outcomes in the Personal Plan that the agency agreed to support.
The QIDP, a DSP and, as needed, a nurse and other professionals who are responsible for service functions in the Personal Plan areas the agency covers and for developing the Implementation Strategy.
Qualified Intellectual Disability Professional, who leads the Provider Support Team and signs the provider signature page.
A planning process directed by the individual that reflects the person's strengths, preferences and goals and supports integration and choice.

procedures: The QIDP receives the Personal Plan from the ISC and logs the date received. The QIDP reads it in full and discusses it with the individual and guardian, in a format and language they understand (IR-07).

The QIDP identifies the outcomes, supports and services in the Personal Plan that the agency agreed to support and confirms that every service the agency will bill is listed in the Personal Plan. If a needed service is missing, or a change is needed, the QIDP tells the ISC in writing.

Within 10 calendar days of receiving the Personal Plan, the QIDP signs and dates the provider signature page and returns it to the ISC. The QIDP records the dates and calendars the 20-day Implementation Strategy due date.

The QIDP convenes the Provider Support Team, which includes the QIDP, a DSP, and a nurse or other professionals as needed, together with the individual, guardian and a representative of the ISC agency. The meeting is held at a time and place convenient to the individual.

The team reviews the Personal Plan and current assessments, including the health risk screening and any risk findings (PCS-03), and plans how the agency will support each outcome the agency agreed to support. The team plans around the person's preferences, schedule and community interests.

The QIDP writes the Implementation Strategy on Form IL462-4470 within 20 calendar days of the QIDP's dated signature on the provider signature page. It covers only the Personal Plan areas the agency agreed to support, states measurable steps, who is responsible, and how progress will be documented, and includes identified health and safety risks.

Where the person needs continuous supervision, any time alone or independent community access is only planned based on the team's assessment of the person's need and preference, not staff convenience, and the strategy states the time periods and locations involved (PCS-06).

The QIDP reviews the strategy with the individual and guardian and answers questions. The individual and guardian sign and date it. DDD guidance states that the ISC does not sign or approve the strategy. The Administrator confirms current practice with BALC and the Department, and the agency follows any written instruction.

The QIDP gives a copy of the strategy to the individual and guardian, and sends a copy to the ISC, within [number of days set by the Administrator, no later than 5 business days] of signature. The QIDP records the date and method of delivery.
The signed strategy is placed in the individual's record. A current copy is kept at the residence where staff can use it, and kept confidential under IR-04.
Direct Support Professionals are trained on each person's strategy before they work alone with the person and whenever it changes. Training is documented on a signed training sheet.

At least monthly, the QIDP reviews the strategy against daily documentation (PCS-04), speaks with the individual and staff, and documents whether supports are being provided, are working, and still match the person's wishes. The QIDP records any needed changes and the date.

The QIDP updates the strategy at least annually to align with the new Personal Plan, and sooner when there is a change in the person's health, behavior, goals, residence or supports, or when the individual or guardian requests it. Updates are signed by the individual and guardian and distributed in the same way as the original strategy.

When the individual or guardian wants a change that goes beyond the agency's agreed supports, or when the person needs a service not in the Personal Plan, the QIDP notifies the ISC in writing so the Personal Plan can be changed. The agency does not bill for the service until it is identified in the Personal Plan.

The QIDP records all planning meetings, including attendees, dates and outcomes. When the individual or guardian disagrees with the strategy or the agency's supports, the disagreement is documented and addressed through IR-03.

The Administrator checks timelines monthly using a tracking sheet: Personal Plan received, signature page returned, strategy due and completed, monthly reviews, and annual updates. Missed timelines are reported to the Administrator at once and corrected, and trends go to quality improvement (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Sign the provider signature page, write and update the Implementation Strategy on time, convene the Provider Support Team, perform monthly reviews and communicate with the ISC.
Plan, deliver and review supports with the individual and guardian, with 24-hour availability as required.
Carry out the strategy as written, document daily, and report barriers or changes to the QIDP.
Contribute health risks and supports to the strategy and review health-related sections.
Track timelines, ensure billing matches the Personal Plan, and resolve late or missing documents.
