policies.title: Assessments, Health Risk Screening and Requests for Additional Supports
policies.applies_to: [AGENCY NAME] QIDPs, nurses, Provider Support Teams, the Administrator and staff who contribute to assessments or support requests
policies.purpose: To identify each person's needs and risks through timely assessment and to make sure the supports and staffing needed are requested from the Department and reviewed regularly.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] assesses each individual on entry and at least annually. Health screening uses the Department's web-based tool, and a paper request is used only with written justification. Identified risks are included in the Implementation Strategy. When the Provider Support Team believes additional staff resources or supports are needed, the agency submits a request to the Department. The Department responds as soon as possible and no later than ten business days after receipt. Need for non-base support hours is professionally reviewed at least annually and the result is reported to the Department. For intermittent supports, the ISC and the agency submit a CILA rate determination packet to the Department.

definitions.definition: A structured review of a person's health and safety risks, completed using the Department's web-based screening tool.
Staff resources, equipment or services beyond the supports funded in the person's current rate that the team believes are needed.
Staffing hours above the base level of support in the person's rate.
The packet submitted by the ISC with the CILA agency for individuals who need intermittent supports so that the Department can determine the rate.

procedures: At entry, the QIDP and nurse assess the person's needs, including health, medication, mobility, communication, behavior, safety, daily living skills, risk and the person's preferences and strengths. Results are written in the record within [number] days, not later than the Implementation Strategy due date in PCS-02.

The nurse and QIDP complete the Department's web-based health risk screening for each person at entry and at least annually, and when the person's condition changes. A paper request is used only when the Administrator documents a written justification and the Department allows it.

The QIDP and nurse record each identified risk, such as choking, seizures, falls, aspiration, medications, behavior and emergency evacuation limits, along with the supports to reduce it. They list every identified risk in the Implementation Strategy (PCS-02) and tie it to HW-03 monitoring where relevant.

The team talks with the individual and guardian about the assessment results, using plain language and the person's preferred communication method, and records the person's views and any disagreement.
The QIDP repeats assessments at least annually, when there is a change in health, behavior or functioning, after a hospitalization, serious incident or fall, or when the individual or guardian asks.

When the Provider Support Team believes the person needs additional staff resources or supports to stay safe or reach the Personal Plan outcomes, the QIDP documents the need, the evidence (assessments, incident data, daily notes, medical opinions) and the amount and type of support requested.

The QIDP drafts the request with the nurse and Administrator, obtains the individual's and guardian's input, and submits it to the Department with the ISC informed. The QIDP records the date submitted and the date the Department received it.

The Administrator tracks each request. The Department must respond as soon as possible and no later than ten business days after receipt. If no response is received within ten business days, the Administrator contacts the Department in writing and records the follow-up.

While a request is pending, the team keeps all current supports in place and adds interim safety measures within the agency's own resources as needed. The agency does not reduce required supervision or support because a request is pending.

When the Department approves, changes or denies a request, the QIDP informs the individual, guardian and ISC in writing, updates the Implementation Strategy, adjusts staffing schedules, and records the date effective. If the request is denied, the QIDP explains the reason and the options for appeal or another request.

At least annually, a qualified professional on the team reviews the person's need for non-base support hours. The review looks at current needs, incident and daily documentation, and any changes in condition or goals. The Administrator reports the results to the Department and records the date reported.

When a person is assessed as needing only intermittent supports, the QIDP works with the ISC to prepare and submit the CILA rate determination packet to the Department. The QIDP provides the agency's portion promptly and records the date submitted.
The Administrator reviews a summary of requests, response times and outcomes quarterly and reports to the governing body through the quality improvement process (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Coordinate assessments, draft and submit requests for additional supports, track Department responses, and update the Implementation Strategy.
Complete the health risk screening, identify health risks and recommend supports.
Approve and track requests, ensure annual non-base hour reviews are reported to the Department, and adjust staffing.
Provide observations and daily data used for assessments, and carry out interim safety measures.
Submit the CILA rate determination packet with the agency for intermittent supports.

documentation: Entry and annual assessments
Health risk screening results (web-based tool) and any written justification for paper requests
Risk entries in the Implementation Strategy
Requests for additional supports with supporting evidence
Dates of submission, Department response and follow-up
Annual non-base support hour review and report to the Department
CILA rate determination packet (intermittent supports)
Notices to the individual, guardian and ISC
Quarterly request summary

policies.title: Implementation of Supports and Daily Documentation
policies.applies_to: All Direct Support Professionals, QIDPs, nurses and program supervisors at every [AGENCY NAME] CILA site
policies.purpose: To make sure each person receives the care, supervision and supports identified through assessment and described in the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy, and that daily delivery of those supports is documented accurately and can be reviewed by the person, the guardian, the ISC, BALC and DDD.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides care and supervision based on each individual's assessed needs and is available to each individual 24 hours a day through the Provider Support Team. Staff deliver supports as written in the Implementation Strategy and document, every shift, the support delivered against each outcome the agency agreed to support. All notes are dated and signed. The QIDP reviews the Implementation Strategy at least monthly and documents the review. Staff report any change in an individual's functional status to the QIDP, who updates the strategy. Each person's record contains the required Part 115 contents, including written informed consent to participate, prior service history, the Personal Plan and the Implementation Strategy. Current copies of the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy are kept at the residence, in paper or digital form, and are available to staff on every shift.

definitions.definition: The team [AGENCY NAME] maintains for each individual. It includes a QIDP and a DSP, plus a nurse or other professionals as needed, and it is responsible for developing and carrying out the Implementation Strategy.
The written plan on Form IL462-4470, based on the Personal Plan and assessments, that states how the agency will support the outcomes it agreed to support.
The person-centered plan developed with the individual, guardian and ISC under 59 Ill. Adm. Code 120 and Part 115.
Qualified Intellectual Disability Professional, the member of the Provider Support Team who develops, monitors and reviews the Implementation Strategy.
Direct Support Professional, the staff member who provides daily hands-on support and documents it.
Any noticeable change in the person's abilities, health, behavior, mood, skills, mobility, communication or support needs, whether a decline or an improvement.

procedures: The QIDP develops the Implementation Strategy on Form IL462-4470 within 20 calendar days of the provider's dated signature on the Personal Plan. The QIDP uses the Personal Plan and assessments and involves the individual and guardian, with the ISC as necessary.
The individual and guardian sign the strategy. The QIDP gives each of them a copy and gives them copies of every update, and documents the date given.

The QIDP files the signed strategy in the individual's record and places a current copy at the residence in the program binder or secure electronic system that staff can access on every shift. The Program Director confirms this at each monthly site check.

The QIDP trains each DSP assigned to the home on the strategy before the DSP works with the individual alone, and again after every update. Staff sign a training acknowledgment kept in the personnel file and the site binder.

Staff provide supervision and support at the level and in the manner the strategy specifies, and a staff member is available to the individual 24 hours a day. Staff do not substitute their own routines for the person's preferences and schedule.

Each shift, the DSP completes a dated, signed daily note for every individual. The note records the supports delivered against each Implementation Strategy outcome, the person's participation and response, community activities, any refusals or choices made, and anything the next shift needs to know.

Notes are written during or at the end of the shift in which the support occurred, in permanent ink or in the electronic record with a user-identified signature. Late entries are marked as late, dated and signed. Staff never alter or delete an entry. Corrections use a single line, with the date and initials.
Staff record objective facts, such as what was offered, what the person did and said, and the amount of assistance given. They avoid conclusions and unflattering labels.
If an outcome was not supported on a shift, the DSP documents the reason (for example, the person declined, illness, or a schedule change) and informs the QIDP by the next business day.
Staff report any change in functional status to the QIDP, and to the nurse when health related, on the same shift. Urgent health matters follow HW-04. The QIDP documents the report and any follow-up.

After a reported change, the QIDP meets with the Provider Support Team, the individual and the guardian as needed, and updates the Implementation Strategy. The QIDP gives the updated strategy to the individual and guardian and replaces the copy at the residence. If the change may need additional supports or a rate request, the QIDP follows PCS-03.

At least monthly, the QIDP reviews the Implementation Strategy against the daily notes and incident reports. The QIDP documents progress, barriers, needed changes and the date of the review, and signs it.

The Program Director reviews a sample of daily notes at least monthly for completeness, signatures, dates and alignment with outcomes. The Program Director documents findings, corrects gaps with staff and reports patterns to the quality improvement process under GOV-04.

The QIDP checks every record at least quarterly for the required contents: written informed consent to participate, prior service history, the Personal Plan, the current Implementation Strategy and monthly reviews. Missing items are obtained or created within 14 days, and the check is documented.
Records are kept confidential and used only as permitted by IR-04. Daily notes are available on request to the individual, the guardian, the ISC and authorized state reviewers.

responsibilities.duty: Delivers supports as written, writes dated and signed daily notes each shift, and reports changes in functional status.
Develops the Implementation Strategy within 20 days, reviews it at least monthly, updates it after changes, distributes copies and audits record contents.
Reviews health-related changes, advises on health supports and contributes to updates of the strategy.
Ensures the strategy is at the residence, audits notes monthly and corrects documentation problems.
Ensures staffing and resources allow supports to be delivered and documented, and that 24-hour availability is maintained.

documentation: Signed Implementation Strategy (Form IL462-4470) and every update, with proof of copies given to the individual and guardian
Daily support notes for each individual, dated and signed
QIDP monthly strategy review documentation
Staff training acknowledgments on each individual's strategy
Reports of change in functional status and follow-up actions
Quarterly record-content checklist (consent, prior service history, Personal Plan, strategy)
Monthly Program Director documentation audit

policies.title: Community Integration and Employment Choice
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] CILA staff, QIDPs and supervisors
policies.purpose: To ensure each individual has real opportunities to take part in community life, seek competitive integrated employment, control personal resources and maintain relationships outside the home, as required for CILA settings and HCBS waiver services.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] supports each individual's integration and full access to the greater community. Staff support time out of the home in non-disability-specific activities the person chooses, such as worship, recreation, education, library, shopping and holidays. Staff also support communication by phone, electronic media and mail, and vacations. [AGENCY NAME] offers employment exploration at least annually through the ISC planning process and records each person's choices in the Personal Plan. Day program authorizations are billed separately from the CILA rate, and staff still cover the home when individuals miss day programming. The agency supports relationships with non-paid community members. Integration is based on the person's preferences, not on staff convenience or the agency's schedule.

definitions.definition: Opportunities for the individual to seek competitive integrated employment, engage in community life and control personal resources, to the same degree as people not receiving HCBS.
Work in the community, at or above minimum wage, alongside people without disabilities, as described in the individual's employment goals.
A community activity that is open to the general public and not designed only for people with disabilities.
A separately authorized and billed service that is not part of the CILA rate.

procedures: At the Personal Plan meeting and at each annual update, the QIDP asks the individual, in the person's preferred communication method, about the community activities, places, faith or cultural practices, learning interests and relationships the person wants. The QIDP records the answers in the Implementation Strategy.

The QIDP and ISC offer employment exploration at least annually through the ISC planning process. The QIDP documents the offer, the person's response and any decision to explore, pursue, continue or decline employment, and records the choices in the Personal Plan.

If the person is interested in employment, the QIDP helps arrange referrals, benefits counseling and supports through the ISC and other service providers. The QIDP documents the referrals and follow-up dates.

The QIDP builds each individual's chosen community activities into a weekly schedule with the individual. The schedule includes activities outside the home that are not disability-specific and at least one activity chosen by the person alone.

Staff support community outings at the times the person chooses. Outings are not limited to group schedules or the agency's vehicle availability, and staff arrange transportation, public transit training or other means so that participation does not depend on staff convenience.

Staff support the person's communication by phone, electronic media and mail, and support planning of vacations and holidays, including help with money and bookings. Limits on communication follow IR-02 only.
Staff support the person's relationships with family, friends, neighbors, coworkers and other non-paid community members. Visitors are welcome under IR-01.
The Administrator ensures that staffing patterns and vehicle schedules allow individuals to attend activities at different times and places, including evenings and weekends.

When an individual misses day program, the Program Director schedules staff so the home is covered with the support the person's Implementation Strategy requires, and no one is told to stay home because of staffing. Day program is billed separately and is never billed to the CILA rate.

Staff document each community activity in the daily note under PCS-04, including where the person went, what the person chose and any barriers. They also document when a person declined, and the person's choice is respected.

The QIDP reviews community participation monthly. If a person has had little time outside the home, the QIDP meets with the person and guardian to identify the cause, such as lack of interest, transport, health or staffing, and revises the strategy.
Staff assist the person in controlling personal resources during community activities, including carrying and spending the person's own money as the person is able, following IR-05.
The Program Director reviews community integration data quarterly and reports barriers and trends to the quality improvement process under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Supports the person's chosen community activities, communications and relationships and documents participation.
Elicits preferences, documents employment choice at least annually, builds activities into the strategy and reviews participation monthly.
Schedules staff and transportation so integration is not limited by staffing and covers the home when day program is missed.
Allocates resources, ensures the agency does not restrict community access for convenience and reviews quarterly integration data.

documentation: Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy sections on community activities and employment choice
Annual employment exploration offer and the person's response
Weekly activity schedules
Daily notes on community participation
QIDP monthly review of community integration
Quarterly integration data summary

policies.title: Time Alone and Independent Community Access
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] CILA staff, QIDPs, nurses and supervisors, and the Provider Support Team
policies.purpose: To allow individuals who need continuous supervision to spend time alone at home or access the community independently when this is safe and consistent with their wishes, through a documented team assessment and individualized plan that protects both autonomy and safety.
policies.policy: A person who needs continuous supervision may stay alone in the home or go into the community independently only under the specific circumstances allowed by 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.230. The Provider Support Team assesses the person's ability and desire. The decision is based on the person's need and preference, never on staff convenience. The Implementation Strategy states the times, locations and time frames involved. Continuous supervision is applied as the strategy specifies, which may range from line of sight to present and accessible. Each plan for time alone or independent access includes an emergency plan and a way for the person to reach staff.

definitions.definition: Staff physically on-site during all hours individuals are present, unless the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy say otherwise.
A level of supervision in which staff can see the person at all times.
A level of supervision in which staff are in the home or immediately available but do not need to see the person at all times.
A planned period when the person is in the home without staff physically present.
A planned period when the person goes into the community without staff accompanying the person.

procedures: Any individual, guardian or team member may ask for time alone or independent community access. Staff who receive a request tell the QIDP within one business day and document it.

The QIDP convenes the Provider Support Team, which includes the person, the guardian, the nurse as needed and the ISC as appropriate, within 14 calendar days of a request. The team reviews the request together.

The team assesses the person's skills and wishes, using observation and the person's own words. Areas include handling emergencies such as fire, medical problems, strangers and lost keys, using a phone, telling time, traffic and transit skills, money skills, medical and seizure risks, and behavior history.

The team documents its assessment and reasoning, and how the decision is based on need and preference and not on staffing levels, schedules or convenience. The team may not deny a request because staff are not available.

If the team supports the request, the QIDP writes the plan into the Implementation Strategy, stating the time periods, locations, maximum length of time, the level of supervision before and after, and when the person will check in.

The plan includes an emergency plan specific to the person and the setting. It describes steps for fire, injury, illness, seizure, getting lost or feeling unsafe, lists contact numbers for staff, the nurse and the guardian, and tells how to call 911.

The plan names the way the person will reach staff, such as a working cell phone, a landline, a medical alert device or a check-in schedule, and states who responds and how quickly. The QIDP checks that the device works before the plan starts.

The QIDP trains the person on the plan in a format the person understands, and trains staff on their roles, including who is the on-call contact. The QIDP documents the training and practices the emergency steps with the person.
The person and guardian sign the updated strategy. The QIDP gives them a copy, files it in the record and places a copy at the residence under PCS-04.

The plan starts with a trial period. Staff document each episode of time alone or independent access in the daily note, including the start and end times, how the person did, any problems and whether check-ins occurred.

The QIDP reviews the episodes at least monthly. The team may expand, adjust or reduce the plan based on the person's experience. Any reduction is explained to the person and guardian and is based on safety, not convenience.

If a person is hurt, in danger or unable to follow the plan, staff respond under the emergency plan and report under HW-04 and the incident reporting procedures. The team meets within seven days to review whether to change the plan.
If the team limits the person's access in a way that restricts a right, the limit is handled under IR-02 and not under this policy.
The Administrator reviews all active time-alone and independent-access plans at least annually, and verifies that none are based on staffing convenience.

responsibilities.duty: Assesses ability and desire, decides based on need and preference, and reviews the plan at least monthly.
Convenes the team, writes the plan with times, locations and time frames, trains staff and the person, and updates the strategy.
Follows the plan, documents each episode and responds to emergencies.
Advises on health, medication and seizure risks relevant to time alone.
Ensures requests are not denied for staffing reasons and reviews plans annually.

documentation: Written request and date received
Provider Support Team assessment and decision rationale
Implementation Strategy section with times, locations, time frames and level of supervision
Emergency plan and means of contacting staff
Training records for the person and staff
Daily notes of each episode and QIDP monthly review
Annual administrator review

policies.title: Respite Services (if offered)
policies.applies_to: [AGENCY NAME] administrators, QIDPs, nurses and DSPs at any site that offers respite. Respite is offered only if marked 'Offered' on the agency's adoption page.
policies.purpose: To make sure any respite stay is safe for the respite guest and for the people who live in the home, and that the health screening, safety review and time limits in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.205 are met.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] offers respite only if this policy is marked 'Offered' on the agency's policy adoption page. If it is marked 'Not offered', the agency provides no respite and all requests are referred to other providers through the ISC. If respite is offered, the agency requires a physician statement that the guest has no contagious disease before the stay begins. The agency documents that the guest will not jeopardize the health or safety of other residents in the home. Respite lasting more than two weeks requires Department approval before the first two weeks end, and is allowed only in emergencies.

definitions.definition: Short-term services provided to a person with a developmental disability in a CILA, typically to give family or other caregivers a break or to meet an emergency.
The person receiving respite in the home who is not a permanent resident.
An illness that can be spread to others in the home and that a physician has not cleared.
A sudden crisis, such as loss of the usual caregiver or home, that requires immediate alternative care.

procedures: The Administrator marks on the policy adoption page whether respite is 'Offered' or 'Not offered'. If not offered, staff who receive a request document it and refer the family to the ISC.

When a respite request is received, the QIDP gathers the guest's guardian and caregiver information, support needs, medications, health conditions, behavior and communication needs, and the requested dates.

Before the stay is approved, the QIDP obtains a signed statement from a physician that the guest has no contagious disease. The statement is dated close to the date of arrival, and a stay does not begin without it.

The QIDP and Program Director review the home's current residents, the guest's needs and the guest's behavior and health history. They document whether the guest will jeopardize the health or safety of others in the home, and they consult the nurse on health matters.
If the review shows a risk to residents that cannot be managed, the Program Director declines the stay and informs the family and the ISC the same day, with the reason documented.

The QIDP informs the residents of the home and, where applicable, their guardians that a respite guest will be staying, including the dates, and honors residents' privacy and rights. Residents' concerns are recorded and addressed.

The QIDP obtains written consent from the guest or guardian for the stay, a list of medications with the prescriber's orders, emergency contacts and any plan or strategy information provided by the home provider.

The Program Director ensures staffing is adequate for the additional person, and the guest has a safe bed and personal space. Rights and rules for the guest follow IR-01 and are explained in a way the person understands.
Medications are given under HW-01. Staff do not give any medication without a current prescriber's order and consent.
Staff document daily support for the guest as in PCS-04. The notes include health, activities, behavior and any incidents.

The Administrator tracks the length of each stay. If a stay will pass two weeks, the Administrator contacts the Department, before the first two weeks end, to request approval. This is done only for an emergency, and the request and decision are documented.

If Department approval is not received before the end of the first two weeks, the agency arranges for the guest to leave on or before the end of the second week, working with the guardian and the ISC.
At the end of the stay, staff return medications and belongings with a signed inventory, give the guardian a summary of the stay and document any incidents or concerns in the record.
The Program Director reviews each respite stay within seven days after its end and reports problems to the quality improvement process under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Decides whether respite is offered, tracks stay length and requests Department approval for emergency stays beyond two weeks.
Gathers information, obtains the physician statement and documents the safety review and consents.
Reviews health information and the physician statement, and advises on medication.
Ensures staffing and space and reviews each stay.
Supports the guest and documents daily.

documentation: Policy adoption page showing 'Offered' or 'Not offered'
Respite request and referral records
Physician statement of no contagious disease
Documented review that the guest will not jeopardize the health or safety of others
Guardian consent, medication orders and emergency contacts
Daily notes and incident reports during the stay
Department approval request and decision, if applicable
Post-stay review

policies.title: Transition, Discharge and Termination of Services
policies.applies_to: [AGENCY NAME] administrators, QIDPs, program directors, nurses and all staff involved in an individual's move or the end of services
policies.purpose: To protect each individual's right to remain in the CILA and to make sure any move or end of services is voluntary or based only on the criteria in the licensing rule, is person-centered, well planned, and respects the person's rights and privacy.
policies.policy: Individuals have the right to remain in the CILA unless they voluntarily withdraw or meet the criteria in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.215, as referenced in 115.250. Termination is never a punitive response to behavior or a way to avoid staffing needs. [AGENCY NAME] coordinates with the ISC, QIDP, individual and guardian and documents the team recommendation. The person and guardian receive written notice and the rights and contact information for the Guardianship and Advocacy Commission (GAC), the Department's Office of the Inspector General (OIG), the Department and Equip for Equality. Records are transferred only with a signed release. The agency plans the transition and follows up after the move. Agency closure is handled under GOV-06.

definitions.definition: A decision by the individual, or the guardian when applicable, to leave the CILA.
An agency-initiated end of CILA services, allowed only under the criteria in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.215.
A written plan covering the move, including the receiving setting, supports, belongings, medications, records and follow-up.
Independent Service Coordination agency that coordinates the individual's services and planning.
Guardianship and Advocacy Commission.
The Department's Office of the Inspector General.

procedures: The Administrator keeps a current copy of the criteria in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.215 and the related notice requirements in the compliance binder. The Administrator reviews it with the QIDPs and Program Directors at orientation and when the rule changes.

If an individual or guardian says they want to leave, staff tell the QIDP the same day. The QIDP meets with the person and guardian within five business days to discuss the reasons, the options and the supports that could address concerns.

The QIDP notifies the ISC and arranges a meeting of the person, guardian, ISC, Provider Support Team and others the person chooses. The team explores what supports might allow the person to stay, if that is what the person wants.
For a voluntary move, the QIDP documents the person's or guardian's decision in writing and begins a transition plan with the receiving provider or family.

If the agency believes a person meets a termination criterion, the Administrator and QIDP first document the specific criterion, the facts and every support or change tried. Termination is not used as a response to behavior, to punish, or to solve staffing, scheduling or rate problems.

Before any notice, the QIDP convenes the Provider Support Team, the individual, guardian and ISC, and requests additional supports or services, including a rate review under PCS-03 where needed. The team's recommendation and the reasons are documented.

The Administrator reviews the recommendation, confirms in writing which criterion in 115.215 applies and consults [LEGAL OR COMPLIANCE CONTACT] as needed. No decision is made by a single staff member.

The agency gives the individual and guardian written notice of the proposed termination, in plain language and accessible format, stating the reason, the criterion relied on, the date and the steps to appeal. The notice follows the time frames required by 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.215.

With the notice, the agency gives the person and guardian the address and telephone number of GAC, OIG, the Department and Equip for Equality, offers to help them make contact and documents that this was done.
The individual continues to receive all services and supports at the agreed level until the transition is complete. Staff do not reduce services or pressure the person to leave.

The QIDP leads transition planning with the person, guardian, ISC and receiving provider. The plan covers the receiving setting, the person's preferences, visits to the new home, transportation, medications and health information, behavior and communication supports, personal belongings and funds, and day and community activities.

The agency transfers records and health information only with a signed release from the person or guardian, as required by IR-04 and the Confidentiality Act. The QIDP documents what was sent, when and to whom.

The nurse gives the receiving provider a medication list, current orders, a supply of medications as allowed, health risks and follow-up appointments. Personal funds and property are accounted for and returned under IR-05, with a signed receipt.
Within 7 days after the move, and again at 30 days, the QIDP contacts the person, guardian and receiving provider to check how the move is going, and documents the contacts and any concerns.

The Administrator closes the record under the agency's retention rules, reports the discharge to DDD and the ISC as required, and includes discharge data in the quality review under GOV-04. If the agency itself is closing, GOV-06 applies.

responsibilities.duty: Approves any termination, confirms the criterion and notice and ensures termination is never used as punishment.
Leads team meetings, transition planning, notices, follow-up and documentation.
Recommends supports to allow the person to remain and documents its recommendation.
Prepares medication and health information for transfer.
Ensures services continue and the transition runs smoothly.

documentation: Individual or guardian statement of intent to withdraw
Team meeting notes and recommendation
Documented criterion under 115.215, with facts and supports tried
Written notice with rights and contact information for GAC, OIG, the Department and Equip for Equality
Transition plan and signed releases of information
Medication and records transfer log, and funds and property receipt
Follow-up contact notes at 7 and 30 days

policies.title: Medication Administration and Staff Certification
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] staff who administer, assist with or supervise medications, and the nurses, QIDPs and supervisors who oversee them
policies.purpose: To ensure medications are prescribed, administered, monitored and documented safely and lawfully, and that only properly trained and certified staff administer medications.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides or supervises medications only in accordance with the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Administrative Act and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 116. A licensed physician (MD or DO) is responsible for medical services, including prescribing. A physician examines the individual before psychotropic medication is started. AIMS screening is completed at least every six months for individuals on psychotropic medication. A physician reviews medications and sees the individual at least every six months, or more often if a psychiatrist requires. Staff help individuals access information about their medications, including observing and reporting effects and side effects. Staff administer medications only after completing the DHS-approved medication administration course and passing score that [AGENCY NAME] has confirmed with BALC as current. The agency uses a medication administration record (MAR), reports errors and incidents to the RN and QIDP, stores medications securely and counts controlled substances.

definitions.definition: The written or electronic record of each medication ordered and each dose given, refused or missed.
A medication prescribed to affect mood, behavior, thinking or perception.
Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale, a screening for movement side effects such as tardive dyskinesia.
Any deviation from the prescriber's order, including a wrong person, drug, dose, route or time, an omitted dose, or a dose given without an order.
A medication in a federal or state schedule that requires special storage and counting.
Voluntary agreement to a treatment after the person or guardian has been given understandable information about it.

procedures: Before any staff member administers medication, the Administrator or RN confirms with BALC the current DHS-approved medication administration course and passing score, and records the date and source. The agency does not rely on older hour counts or outdated materials.

Staff complete the approved course and meet the passing score before administering any medication. The RN or training coordinator documents the completion date, score, trainer and expiration or renewal date in the personnel file, and the staff member does not give medication until this is on file.

New DSPs are also trained as required under the New Provider Guidance, including DSP training, first aid and CPR and abuse and neglect training, with their completion dates tracked under the agency's personnel procedures.

The RN verifies that each staff member can demonstrate safe administration, including the rights of medication administration, hand hygiene, documentation and what to do in an error, before the staff member administers medication unsupervised. The RN documents the competency check.

A licensed physician (MD or DO) is responsible for each individual's medical services, including prescribing. Staff give medications only on a current, written order from a prescriber, and they do not change a dose or stop a medication on their own.

Before a psychotropic medication is started, a physician examines the individual. The QIDP and RN confirm the exam and obtain informed consent from the individual or guardian under IR-06 before the first dose, and document both.

The RN arranges for AIMS screening at least every six months for each person on psychotropic medication and documents the results. Abnormal findings are reported to the prescriber within one business day.

The RN schedules a physician review of medications, with the physician seeing the individual, at least every six months, or more often if a psychiatrist requires. The RN documents the date, orders and any changes.

Staff keep a MAR for each individual that lists the medication, dose, route, time, prescriber, purpose and known side effects. Staff initial each dose immediately after giving it, and record refusals, held doses and the reason.

Staff observe each person for effects and side effects and report them to the RN on the same shift. They help the person understand their medications in a way the person understands, including what each is for. Staff document these observations in the daily note.

Medications are stored in a locked area and kept in original labeled containers. Medications requiring refrigeration are stored in a secure, temperature-monitored location. Individuals who are assessed as able to self-administer may keep their own medications as allowed by the plan.

Controlled substances are kept under double lock. Two staff count them at each shift change and sign the count log. A discrepancy is reported to the Program Director and RN immediately, and an incident report is completed the same day.

Staff report any medication error, omission, wrong dose or adverse reaction immediately to the RN or on-call nurse, who directs follow-up with the prescriber or poison control as needed. Emergencies follow HW-04. Staff complete an incident report the same shift and notify the QIDP.

The RN reviews medication errors with the staff member within three business days, provides retraining when needed, and removes a staff member from medication duty until competency is re-established. The RN documents the review.
The RN audits MARs, counts, storage and orders at least monthly and reports results and error trends to the quality improvement process under GOV-04.
Medication records are confidential health information. Staff safeguard MARs and prescriptions under IR-04 and the HIPAA privacy standards in 45 CFR 164.530, and share them only as permitted.

responsibilities.duty: Is responsible for medical services and prescribing, examines individuals before psychotropics start and reviews medications at least every six months.
Verifies staff certification and competency, arranges AIMS and physician reviews, reviews errors and audits medication records monthly.
Administers medications as ordered, documents each dose on the MAR, observes and reports effects and secures medications.
Confirms consent and exams, coordinates with the RN and updates the strategy when medication changes affect supports.
Confirms the current approved course with BALC, ensures only certified staff administer and supports the monthly audit.

documentation: BALC confirmation of the current approved course and passing score
Staff certificates, scores, competency checks and renewal dates
Physician orders, psychotropic exam records and informed consents
AIMS screening records every six months
Physician medication review notes
MARs, controlled-substance count logs and storage checks
Medication error and incident reports, and RN follow-up
Monthly RN medication audit

policies.title: Nursing Oversight and Health Care Coordination
policies.applies_to: Authorized CILA agency representative, Administrator, QIDP, agency RN, medication-certified direct support staff, and all staff who support an individual's health care at any [AGENCY NAME] CILA site.
policies.purpose: To make sure each person supported by [AGENCY NAME] receives health care that is overseen by a qualified Illinois-licensed registered nurse, is coordinated with the person's physician and the Provider Support Team, and meets the medical services and medication requirements of 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] employs or contracts with a registered nurse (RN) who holds an unencumbered Illinois license and who has completed the DHS/Division of Developmental Disabilities (DDD) RN trainer webinars required of new CILA providers. The RN is part of the Provider Support Team when the person's needs call for nursing input (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.220). Direct support professionals (DSPs) work under the supervision of the QIDP, the nurse or another authorized higher-level supervisor (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120). The RN trains and oversees staff who administer medication, reviews health risk screening results, and coordinates physician care. A licensed physician (MD/DO) is responsible for each person's medical services, including prescribing. When agency employees provide medical services or medications, or supervise their administration, the agency does so under the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Administrative Act and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 116 (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.240). The person and the guardian, if any, make health care decisions with support, and nursing oversight never replaces their right to consent or refuse (see IR-06).

definitions.definition: A nurse with an unencumbered Illinois RN license, verified on the Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (IDFPR) license lookup, who has completed the DHS/DDD RN trainer webinars.

The team the agency maintains for each individual. It includes a QIDP and a DSP, plus a nurse or other professionals as needed, and it develops the Implementation Strategy (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.220).
A staff member who provides direct care and support to individuals under the supervision of the QIDP, a nurse or another authorized higher-level supervisor (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120).
Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale, a screening for movement side effects, completed at least every six months for individuals taking psychotropic medication (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.240).
The agency's plan, written on Form IL462-4470, for how it will support the outcomes in the individual's Personal Plan, including health risks identified in screening.

procedures: Before hiring or contracting with an RN, the Administrator confirms on the IDFPR license lookup that the nurse holds an active, unencumbered Illinois RN license. The Administrator prints or saves the verification and places it in the personnel file.

The Administrator confirms that the RN has completed the DHS/DDD RN trainer webinars and files the completion record in the personnel file. The RN does not train medication staff until this is on file.

The Administrator re-verifies the RN's license at each renewal period and at least annually. If the license becomes encumbered, lapses or is suspended, the RN stops performing nursing functions immediately and the Administrator arranges a replacement RN the same day.

The Administrator names the RN in writing as the agency's nurse for each site and records the RN's contact information on the site's emergency contact list. The RN's duties are set out in a written job description or contract.

The RN reviews each new person's health history, physician orders, medication list and health risk screening during admission (see PCS-01 and PCS-03). The RN documents recommendations in writing for the QIDP and Provider Support Team.

The QIDP includes the RN in Provider Support Team meetings when health needs are identified. The RN's recommendations are written into the Implementation Strategy so that health risks in the Personal Plan are addressed (see PCS-02 and PCS-03).

The RN trains staff who will administer or assist with medication, assesses their competence and oversees their practice as set out in HW-01. The RN documents each training and observation in the staff member's training record.

The RN makes sure a licensed physician is identified for each person. The RN confirms that a physician examines the person before any psychotropic medication starts, and that the person is seen and medications are reviewed by a physician at least every six months, or more often if a psychiatrist requires.

The RN tracks the date of each person's last and next physician visit and AIMS screening on a health calendar kept at the site. AIMS screening is completed at least every six months for each person taking psychotropic medication, and the results go to the prescribing physician.

Before each appointment, the RN or QIDP gives staff a written list of the questions and concerns to raise. Staff bring the current medication list, face sheet and the Personal Plan health summary to the appointment.

After each appointment, the DSP who accompanied the person records the outcome and any new orders on the appointment form the same day. The RN reviews new orders within one business day and arranges for the medication administration record, protocols and Implementation Strategy to be updated as needed.

The RN reviews medication administration records, medication errors and observed effects and side effects at least monthly. The RN reports concerns to the prescribing physician and the QIDP, and documents the review.

The RN shares health information with the ISC, the guardian and other providers only as permitted by IR-04, and only with required consents. The QIDP and RN make sure the person and guardian receive the health information they ask for in an understandable form.
When a person has a change of condition, staff call the RN under HW-04. The RN assesses the person by phone or in person, directs follow-up and documents the contact.
The QIDP reviews the Implementation Strategy at least monthly and consults the RN on any health-related outcome or support. The review is documented as required by PCS-02.

The Administrator reviews RN oversight activities (license verification, trainings, physician visit tracking, AIMS completion) quarterly as part of the quality improvement review in GOV-04, and corrects any gaps found.

responsibilities.duty: Hires and verifies the RN's license and training, keeps those records current, and makes sure nursing oversight is available for every site.
Trains and oversees medication staff, reviews health risk screening, coordinates physician visits and AIMS screening, assesses changes in condition, and documents nursing oversight.
Includes nursing recommendations in the Implementation Strategy, reviews it monthly, and keeps the Provider Support Team informed of health needs.
Follows physician and RN orders and protocols, brings required documents to appointments, records outcomes, and reports health concerns to the RN promptly.
Makes sure the agency maintains qualified nursing oversight and resources for health care coordination.

documentation: RN IDFPR license verification (initial and renewal) and DHS/DDD RN trainer webinar completion record
RN job description or contract
Health risk screening review and RN recommendations in the individual record
Physician visit and AIMS screening tracking calendar, and AIMS results
Appointment forms and new physician orders
Medication staff training and observation records
Monthly RN medication and health review notes
Provider Support Team meeting notes and monthly Implementation Strategy review notes
Quarterly quality improvement review of nursing oversight

policies.title: Health Monitoring, Seizures and Choking Risk
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] staff who support individuals, the agency RN, the QIDP and the Administrator at every CILA site.
policies.purpose: To make sure each person's health is routinely monitored and that individual risks such as seizures, choking, dysphagia and aspiration are identified, addressed in the Implementation Strategy, and managed through written protocols that every staff member is trained on before working alone.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] monitors each person's health based on assessed needs and the physician's and RN's orders. Health risks found in health risk screening and the Personal Plan are addressed in the person's Implementation Strategy (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.230; see PCS-03). The agency writes an individual protocol for each person with a seizure disorder, choking risk, dysphagia or aspiration risk, based on the RN's assessment and physician orders. All staff are trained on each protocol before they work alone with that person. Staff keep first aid and CPR certification current and renew it every two years. Care and supervision are provided based on assessed needs, and the team observes and reports medication effects and side effects (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.220). Health monitoring respects the person's dignity, privacy and choices.

definitions.definition: A structured review of a person's health needs and risks that is used to plan supports and is reviewed by the RN (see PCS-03).

A written, individual plan from the RN and physician orders that describes the person's seizure types, what staff do during and after a seizure, when to give any ordered rescue medication, and when to call 911.
Difficulty swallowing.
Food, liquid, saliva or other material entering the airway or lungs.
A written, individual plan from the RN and physician or other clinician orders describing food textures, liquid consistency, positioning, mealtime supervision and emergency response.

procedures: At admission and at least annually, the RN reviews each person's health history, diagnoses, orders and screening results for seizure, choking, dysphagia, aspiration and other health risks. The RN gives written findings to the QIDP.
The QIDP makes sure each identified health risk is addressed in the Implementation Strategy, and that the strategy names who is responsible and how staff will monitor it (see PCS-02 and PCS-03).

For each person with a seizure disorder, the RN writes an individual seizure protocol from the physician's orders. It lists seizure types and triggers, first aid steps, rescue medication orders, when to call 911 and whom to notify.

For each person with a choking, dysphagia or aspiration risk, the RN writes an individual protocol from physician and clinician orders (such as speech-language pathology). It lists diet texture, liquid consistency, positioning, pacing, mealtime supervision level and emergency steps. A copy is kept in the kitchen or dining area and in the individual record.
The RN reviews each protocol with the physician at least at every six-month physician visit and updates it after any seizure with injury, choking event, hospitalization or change in orders.

Before any staff member works alone with a person who has a protocol, the RN or a person the RN has trained teaches the protocol and observes the staff member demonstrate it. The trainer and staff member sign and date the training record.

The Administrator keeps proof that each staff member holds current first aid and CPR certification, renewed every two years. A staff member whose certification lapses is not scheduled alone until it is renewed.

During a seizure, staff follow the protocol, protect the person from injury, note the time, observe and record the seizure on the seizure record, and call 911 when the protocol says to or when the person is in danger. See HW-04 for emergency steps.

Staff record each seizure on the seizure record (date, start and end time, description, triggers, recovery and any rescue medication). They notify the RN as the protocol directs, and the RN reviews the records at least monthly and shares trends with the physician.
At each meal, staff follow the diet, positioning and supervision requirements in the protocol. Staff never change a texture, liquid consistency or supervision level without a written order.
If a person chokes, staff follow the choking protocol and emergency first aid and call 911 when required. Every choking event is reported to the RN and QIDP the same day and handled under HW-04.

Staff measure and record vital signs and weights on the schedule ordered by the physician or set by the RN, using the form kept in the individual record. Staff report readings outside the ranges set by the RN right away.
Staff record every medical, dental and other health appointment, including the date, provider, outcome and follow-up, in the individual record.
The QIDP and RN share health information with the ISC, physician and other providers as the Personal Plan requires and as permitted by IR-04.
Staff observe and report medication effects and side effects to the RN so the physician can respond (see HW-01 and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.220).
The Administrator reviews seizure, choking, weight and health monitoring trends quarterly under GOV-04 and acts on patterns.

responsibilities.duty: Assesses risks, writes seizure and choking/dysphagia/aspiration protocols from physician orders, trains staff, and reviews monitoring records at least monthly.
Makes sure health risks are addressed in the Implementation Strategy, coordinates the Provider Support Team, and confirms protocols are in the record.
Follows each individual's protocols, records seizures, vital signs and weights, supervises meals as ordered and reports concerns right away.
Makes sure no staff member works alone before protocol training and current first aid/CPR, and that training records are kept.

documentation: Health risk screening and RN risk review
Individual seizure protocols and choking/dysphagia/aspiration protocols with physician orders
Staff protocol training records (signed and dated)
First aid and CPR certificates with expiration dates
Seizure records and choking event records
Vital sign and weight logs
Appointment records and information-sharing documentation
Monthly RN review notes and quarterly quality improvement review

policies.title: Change of Condition and Emergency Medical Care
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] staff, the agency RN, the QIDP, the Administrator and the authorized CILA agency representative at every CILA site.
policies.purpose: To make sure staff recognize and respond quickly to a change in a person's condition or a medical emergency, get the person appropriate care, notify the right people, and report critical incidents as Illinois requires.
policies.policy: Staff respond immediately to any change in a person's health or any medical or psychiatric emergency. Staff call 911 first for any life-threatening event, then notify the RN, QIDP, guardian and ISC. Medical emergencies, unscheduled hospitalizations, injuries of known or unknown origin, and law enforcement or fire department involvement are critical incidents (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120) and are reported through CIRAS. Staff and individuals are trained to react to medical and psychiatric emergencies and poison control (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.300). Each site has an operational telephone that is accessible to staff and individuals, and the site phone number and the nearest poison control center are posted next to it. Any use of restraint in an emergency is governed by 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.245; prone, supine and mechanical restraint are prohibited, and any use must be reported in CIRAS and to the Office of the Inspector General.

definitions.definition: Any new or worsening sign, symptom, behavior, injury or function that differs from the person's usual baseline, whether or not it seems serious.

An event defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120 that must be reported, including medical emergencies, unscheduled hospitalizations, injuries of known or unknown origin, abuse, neglect, exploitation, and law enforcement or fire department involvement.
The Critical Incident Reporting and Analysis System through which critical incidents are reported.
A one-page summary of the person's identifying information, diagnoses, allergies, guardian and emergency contacts, physician and insurance.

procedures: Staff who notice a change of condition stay with the person, assess safety, and follow the person's protocols (see HW-03). They do not wait to see if the problem passes when the signs are serious or the protocol calls for emergency care.

For any life-threatening event (such as unresponsiveness, trouble breathing, choking not resolved, seizure beyond the protocol limit, chest pain, severe bleeding, or suspected stroke or overdose), staff call 911 first and give first aid or CPR as trained until help arrives.

For non-life-threatening changes, staff call the RN right away, give the RN a clear description (what, when, vital signs, usual baseline) and follow the RN's directions. If the RN cannot be reached, staff call the on-call supervisor or the person's physician, or call 911 if the person's condition worsens.
Staff call Poison Control, using the number posted by the site phone, for any suspected poisoning or medication overdose, and follow its directions. Staff call 911 if the person has serious symptoms.

For a psychiatric or behavioral emergency, staff use the person's behavior support plan and de-escalation strategies. Staff call 911 or the crisis resource named in the plan when there is immediate danger. Staff never use prone, supine or mechanical restraint. Any other restraint is used only as permitted by 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.245 and the person's approved plan, and every use is reported in CIRAS and to the Office of the Inspector General (see IR-02).

Before emergency personnel transport the person, staff send or give them the face sheet, current medication list and allergies, and the Personal Plan summary. A staff member accompanies the person or follows to the hospital as soon as staffing allows, while keeping the required supervision for other individuals at the site.

Staff notify the RN, QIDP, Administrator, guardian (or the person's chosen contact if no guardian) and the ISC as soon as the emergency is under control. Staff record each call and the time in the incident record.
Staff protect the person's rights and preferences during treatment and, with the person's and guardian's consent, share the information needed for care with emergency providers (see IR-04 and IR-06).

The Administrator or designee enters each critical incident in CIRAS, and reports any incident that must go to the Office of the Inspector General, within the deadlines in the current DDD and OIG instructions. The Administrator keeps those instructions in the site incident reporting binder.

Staff write an incident report before the end of their shift. It states facts only: what was seen, times, actions taken, who was called, who responded and the person's condition. The report is signed and dated.

For any injury of unknown origin, staff preserve relevant information, note the injury's location and appearance on the body map, and tell the Administrator right away so the Administrator can determine whether abuse or neglect must be reported (see GOV-04 and the agency's abuse and neglect policies).

After a hospital visit or hospitalization, the RN obtains discharge instructions and new orders, updates the medication administration record and protocols, and informs all staff before the person returns to routine care. The QIDP records the information in the person's record.

The QIDP convenes the Provider Support Team after any emergency or hospitalization, updates the Implementation Strategy for any new risks, supports or health needs, and shares updates with the person and guardian (see PCS-02).

The Administrator checks at least quarterly that each site has a working, accessible telephone with the site number and nearest poison control center posted, that first aid kits are stocked, and that staff know how to respond to medical emergencies (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.300). New staff are shown these locations during orientation, and new individuals are trained within 30 days of moving in.
The Administrator reviews each critical incident and trend of changes of condition under GOV-04 and records any corrective action.

responsibilities.duty: Recognizes changes of condition, calls 911 and the RN as required, gives first aid, accompanies or follows the person as staffing allows, and writes the incident report.
Provides telephone and on-site assessment, directs follow-up, reviews discharge orders and updates protocols and medication records.
Notifies the guardian and ISC, convenes the Provider Support Team after an incident and updates the Implementation Strategy.
Makes sure critical incidents are reported through CIRAS and to the OIG within required deadlines, and checks emergency equipment and posted information.
Makes sure the agency maintains 24-hour on-call coverage and resources for emergency response.

documentation: Incident reports and change of condition notes
Notification log (911, RN, QIDP, guardian, ISC, Administrator) with times
CIRAS entries and any OIG reports
Face sheet and medication list sent with the person
Hospital or emergency discharge instructions and new orders
Updated Implementation Strategy and Provider Support Team notes
Quarterly emergency equipment and posted information checks
Training records for emergency response

policies.title: Death of an Individual
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] staff, the agency RN, the QIDP, the Administrator and the authorized CILA agency representative at every CILA site.
policies.purpose: To make sure staff respond to the death of a person supported by [AGENCY NAME] with dignity, immediate and proper emergency action, accurate notification and reporting, protection of records and property, and support for the person's family, housemates and staff.
policies.policy: The death of an individual is a critical incident (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120). Deaths reportable under 59 Ill. Adm. Code Part 50 are reported to the Office of the Inspector General (OIG), and deaths not otherwise reportable are still reported through the critical incident process. Staff are trained on how to respond to a death (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.300). [AGENCY NAME] treats the person with dignity, notifies the guardian or next of kin without delay, preserves records and the scene as needed, and does not release belongings or funds except under written authorization and applicable law (see IR-05).

definitions.definition: An event reportable under 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120, which includes the death of an individual.
A death that must be reported to the Office of the Inspector General under 59 Ill. Adm. Code Part 50, including deaths where abuse, neglect or exploitation is alleged or suspected.
The person's guardian, or the family member or other person the individual has identified to be contacted, as recorded in the person's file.
The agency's review of a death to learn about care, supports and any system improvements (see GOV-04).

procedures: When staff find a person who is unresponsive or not breathing, they call 911 immediately and begin CPR and first aid unless there is a valid, current do-not-resuscitate or POLST order in the record. They follow the dispatcher's instructions until responders take over.

Staff give emergency responders the face sheet, medication list and any advance directive, POLST or DNR order. They follow the directions of emergency responders, law enforcement and the coroner or medical examiner.

Once the death has been pronounced or is clear, staff avoid disturbing the scene beyond what life-saving care required. They leave medications, equipment and the person's surroundings as they are for law enforcement and the coroner or medical examiner, and keep housemates away from the area with care and respect.

The staff member in charge calls the Administrator and the RN right away, and the Administrator calls the authorized CILA agency representative. They arrange additional staff to stay at the site so that all other individuals continue to receive supervision.

The QIDP or Administrator notifies the guardian or next of kin immediately, in person or by phone, with compassion and using only confirmed facts. If the guardian cannot be reached, staff keep trying and record each attempt. Staff do not share news of the death with housemates or unrelated third parties before the family is told, except as needed for the immediate emergency.

The Administrator or designee notifies the ISC and DDD as required and enters the death in CIRAS within the deadline in the current DDD and OIG instructions. The Administrator reports to the OIG any death reportable under Part 50 and makes sure any death not otherwise reportable is still reported through the critical incident process.

If the circumstances suggest possible abuse, neglect, exploitation or an injury of unknown origin, the Administrator reports to the OIG under Part 50 without waiting for the coroner's findings. Staff cooperate fully with investigators and law enforcement and do not alter or discard any record.

Staff who witnessed or responded to the death write a factual statement before the end of their shift, covering what they saw, times, actions taken, who was called and who arrived. Each statement is signed and dated.

The Administrator secures and keeps the person's record, medication administration records, incident reports, protocols and logs in their current state. The Administrator copies them for investigators as needed and does not alter or destroy any original record.

The RN secures the person's medications and counts and documents them with a second staff member. Medications are held until the RN, the physician or the coroner or medical examiner directs how to handle them. Medication administration is stopped and the physician's orders are discontinued.

The body is released only to the funeral home authorized by the guardian or next of kin and cleared by the coroner or medical examiner. Staff do not arrange the funeral or make decisions for the family unless the family asks for help.

The Administrator holds the person's belongings, personal funds and property in a secure place. They are released only to the person authorized in writing under applicable law (see IR-05) and are inventoried with a witness. The agency releases funds in line with IR-05 and state law, and does not dispose of items on its own.

The QIDP and Administrator offer emotional support to housemates, in a way they can understand and that respects their cultural and personal wishes, and offer support to staff. The QIDP updates the Implementation Strategies of housemates for any support needs identified.
With the guardian's and family's agreement, the agency supports housemates and staff who wish to attend services or hold a remembrance.
The Administrator notifies the ISC and Medicaid billing staff so that waiver billing stops as of the date of death and the person's record is closed under GOV-05 and PCS-08.
The authorized CILA agency representative convenes a mortality review under GOV-04 and documents findings, system improvements and corrective actions. The review is shared with the governing body.
The Administrator keeps the complete death file, including notification logs, CIRAS and OIG reports, statements and review findings, for the retention period required by law and agency policy.

responsibilities.duty: Calls 911, gives CPR and first aid as appropriate, preserves the scene, notifies the Administrator and RN, and writes a factual statement.
Secures and counts medications, discontinues orders, advises on clinical review and supports the investigation and mortality review.
Notifies the guardian or next of kin and ISC, supports housemates and updates their plans.
Makes sure CIRAS and OIG reports are made on time, secures records and belongings, coordinates with the coroner and law enforcement and closes the person's record.
Oversees the agency response, convenes the mortality review and reports findings to the governing body.

documentation: Incident reports and staff statements
Notification log with times (guardian or next of kin, ISC, DDD, Administrator, RN)
CIRAS entry and any OIG report
Coroner or medical examiner and law enforcement contact record
Medication count and disposition record
Inventory and release record for belongings and funds, with signed authorization
Copy of the complete individual record kept as originals
Mortality review findings and corrective action
Record closure and billing stop documentation
